definition_zh: 潜在的；潜藏的；潜伏的；休眠的
definition_en: present but not yet visible, active, or developed, and able to appear later
core_image: 一粒埋在土里的种子，看不见，却随时准备破土
scene: 医生看完片子，指着肺部的一处阴影。The scan showed a latent infection that had not yet caused any symptoms.
sceneCN: 这里 latent 是「潜伏的、尚未发作的」（第 2 个义项：疾病或状态潜伏而不显现）；句意：扫描显示有一处尚未引起任何症状的潜伏性感染。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词 latent 加后缀 -cy 构成，指潜伏状态，引申为计算机「延迟」
latent 加副词后缀 -ly，意为「潜在地；潜伏地」
拉丁语 de- + latescere 构成，表示隐藏不露，与 latent 同根，多用于医学潜伏
拉丁语 patere（敞开、显露）与 latere 相对，意为显性的、公开的；在专利义上另有来源

senses.title: Existing but not yet developed or active
senses.definition: existing in a hidden or undeveloped form that could become active or visible later
senses.definitionCN: 以隐藏或未发展的形式存在着，日后可能变得活跃或显现
senses.example: The company is looking for ways to unlock latent demand in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 公司正在寻找办法，开发农村地区的潜在需求。
senses.why: The Latin verb latere means to lie hidden, so the adjective names whatever is lying low and has not yet come out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 latere 意为「隐藏躺着」，所以这个词指藏在低处、尚未露面的东西。

senses.title: Present in a body without symptoms
senses.definition: used of an infection or condition that is present in the body but is not yet causing signs or symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 指感染或病状已存在于体内，但尚未引起症状或体征
senses.example: Some viruses can remain latent in nerve cells for many years.
senses.exampleCN: 一些病毒能在神经细胞中潜伏多年。
senses.why: Medicine borrows the image of hiddenness for a pathogen that hides inside the body instead of showing itself.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「隐藏」的意象，指藏在体内而不显形的病原体。

senses.title: Able to be brought out with effort
senses.definition: used of an ability or quality that a person or place possesses but has not yet used or shown
senses.definitionCN: 指人或地方具备却尚未使用或展现的能力或品质
senses.example: Good teachers help students discover their latent talent.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师帮助学生发现自己潜在的才能。
senses.why: If something lies hidden, it still exists; the ability sense simply points at the hidden half of a skill.
senses.whyCN: 藏起来并不意味着不存在；能力义项正是把技能中「藏起来的那一半」指出来。

senses.title: Stored heat that is not felt as temperature
senses.definition: heat that is absorbed or released when a substance changes state without any change in temperature
senses.definitionCN: 物质发生状态变化时吸收或放出、而温度不变的那部分热量
senses.example: Much of the latent heat released when water turns to ice keeps lakes from freezing quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 水结冰时放出的大量潜热，使湖泊不至于很快冻透。
senses.why: In physics the hidden energy of a change of state is named with the same word, because the heat is present but not felt as temperature.
senses.whyCN: 物理学用同一个词命名状态变化中「藏起来」的能量，因为热能存在却不表现为温度。

senses.title: Dormant and ready to revive
senses.definition: used of seeds, buds, or organisms that are alive but not growing actively
senses.definitionCN: 指种子、芽或生物体仍然存活，但未积极生长
senses.example: These seeds stay latent in the soil until the first heavy rain.
senses.exampleCN: 这些种子在土壤中保持休眠，直到第一场大雨来临。
senses.why: A sleeping seed is the clearest picture of hiddenness in nature: life is there, activity is not.
senses.whyCN: 休眠的种子是大自然中最直观的「隐藏」画面：生命还在，活动却暂停了。

senses.title: Not yet visible in an image
senses.definition: used of an image that has been recorded in a photographic film or sensor but has not yet been developed or seen
senses.definitionCN: 指已记录在胶片或感光元件上、但尚未显影或呈现的影像
senses.example: A chemical bath turns the latent image on the film into a visible picture.
senses.exampleCN: 化学显影液把胶片上的潜影变成可见的图像。
senses.why: Photography keeps the same idea in a technical phrase for a picture that exists chemically but cannot yet be seen.
senses.whyCN: 摄影把同一思路用于技术术语，指已经化学成象却还看不见的照片。

intro.en: Latent comes from Latin latere, to lie hidden, through the present participle latens, which gave the form latentem and then the English adjective.
intro.cn: latent 来自拉丁语 latere（隐藏、躲藏），经现在分词 latens 的形式进入英语形容词。

items.en: Latere means to lie hidden, to lurk, or to keep out of sight.
items.cn: latere 意为隐藏、潜伏或避开视线。

items.en: The present participle latens, stem latent-, means lying hidden.
items.cn: 现在分词 latens（词干 latent-）意为「隐藏着的」。

items.en: Medieval Latin uses latent- in philosophical writing about hidden causes and qualities.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语中，latent- 用于讨论隐藏的原因与性质的哲学写作。

items.en: English takes the adjective into medicine and natural philosophy, where it describes hidden qualities and diseases.
items.cn: 英语在医学与自然哲学中吸收这个形容词，用来描述隐藏的特质与疾病。

items.en: Physics and photography add latent heat and latent image, both openly marked as figurative extensions.
items.cn: 物理与摄影加上「潜热」「潜影」两义，两者都是明显的比喻延伸。

note.en: Latent sits in the hidden family of Latin latere, and stands beside words for things that are dormant, possible, or sleeping.
note.cn: latent 属于拉丁语 latere 的「隐藏」词族，并与表示休眠、可能、沉睡的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of being hidden or the delay before something happens
in a latent way
the Latin form meaning lying hidden
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语现在分词，意为隐藏着的

entries.definition: hidden, especially of a disease that is not showing
entries.definitionCN: 潜伏的（尤指疾病未显症状）

entries.definition: alive or present but not active, as a sleeping volcano is
existing in possibility rather than in act
kept out of sight or not known
not openly shown or admitted

normalIntro.en: Latent is a lying-down word: Latin latere means to lie hidden, so the adjective always points at something that is there but not out in the open.
normalIntro.cn: latent 是「躺着」的词：拉丁语 latere 意为隐藏躺着，因此这个词总是指存在的、却未露面的东西。

normal.en: Compare latency: latency is the noun for the hidden state or for delay, latent is the adjective.
normal.cn: 对比 latency：latency 是表示潜伏状态或延迟的名词，latent 是形容词。

normal.en: Latent heat is the heat that changes ice to water without raising the temperature.
normal.cn: latent heat 指让冰化成水却不升高温度的那部分热。

normal.en: A latent talent is an ability that is there but has not yet been used.
normal.cn: latent talent 指已经具备却尚未使用的才能。

normal.en: A latent infection is present in the body but is not making anyone ill yet.
normal.cn: latent infection 指已在体内、却尚未使人发病的感染。

normal.en: Latent image is a photography term for a picture that is recorded but not yet developed.
normal.cn: latent image 是摄影术语，指已记录却尚未显影的照片。

abstract.en: Picture a seed under the soil: the green shoot is already inside, but nothing shows.
abstract.cn: 想象泥土下的一粒种子：嫩芽早已在里头，却什么也看不见。

abstract.en: Imagine a switch in a dark room: it exists and connects, but nobody has pressed it.
abstract.cn: 想象黑屋里的一只开关：它存在也能通电，却没人按下去。

abstract.en: Think of a volcano with no smoke: the fire is asleep inside the mountain.
abstract.cn: 想象一座不冒烟的火山：火正在山体里沉睡。

examples.en: The virus can lie latent in the body for years before causing symptoms.
examples.cn: 这种病毒可以在体内潜伏多年才引发症状。

examples.en: Heat was applied slowly to unlock the latent energy in the fuel.
examples.cn: 热量被缓慢施加，以释放燃料中的潜在能量。

examples.en: Her latent talent for design was only discovered in her final year.
examples.cn: 她潜在的设计才能直到毕业那年才被发现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「累腾特」——累到趴在床上「躺」着不动，力量藏着不发；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 latere（隐藏、躲藏）→ 现在分词 latens（隐藏着的）→ 英语 latent，核心义「藏着未露」。

sensesIntro.en: Latent begins with anything that exists while hidden, then moves into medicine, ability, physics, botany, and photography, where the same hiddenness gets a technical name.
sensesIntro.cn: latent 先指隐藏而存在的东西，再扩展到医学、能力、物理、植物学与摄影：同一种「隐藏」在每个领域都得到了技术性的名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed lying under the soil, unseen but alive.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒埋在土下的种子，看不见却活着。

branches.en: General hidden existence is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 普遍的隐藏存在是日常义项。

branches.en: A hidden pathogen is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 隐藏的病原体是医学义项。

branches.en: An unused ability is the sense about people.
branches.cn: 未使用的才能是与人有关的义项。

branches.en: Hidden energy behind a change of state is the physics sense.
branches.cn: 状态变化背后隐藏的能量是物理义项。

branches.en: Seed, volcano, and film all hide life or image in a sleeping form.
branches.cn: 种子、火山与胶片都以沉睡的形式藏起生命或影像。

intro.en: Latent is built on the Latin verb latere, and English gathers latency, latently, and the rare delitescent around it.
intro.cn: latent 建立在拉丁动词 latere 之上，英语围绕它构成 latency、latently 以及少见的 delitescent。

latinIntro.en: Latin latere means to lie hidden, and its participle latens supplies the English stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 latere 意为隐藏躺着，其分词 latens 提供了英语词干。

items.example: Latere gives the core image of lying unseen.
items.exampleCN: latere 提供「躺着不被看见」的核心意象。

items.example: The participle latens becomes the English stem latent-.
items.exampleCN: 分词 latens 成为英语词干 latent-。

items.example: Latent is the direct borrowing.
items.exampleCN: latent 是直接借入的形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -cy forms latency.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -cy 构成 latency。

items.example: Latency also names computer delay.
items.exampleCN: latency 也指计算机延迟。

items.meaningCN: 表示「以……方式」的副词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ly forms latently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 latently。

items.example: Latently describes hidden action.
items.exampleCN: latently 描述隐藏发生的作用。

items.example: The prefix de- appears in delitescere and delitescent.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 出现在 delitescere 与 delitescent 中。

items.example: Delitescere intensifies the hiding idea.
items.exampleCN: delitescere 强化了「隐藏」之意。

items.example: Delitescent is a rare medical doublet of latent.
items.exampleCN: delitescent 是 latent 少见的医学同源变体。

definition_zh: 侧面的；横向的；旁边的；横向移动（动词）；侧线（医学术语）
definition_en: relating to the side of something, or moving or extending sideways rather than forward and back
core_image: 一个人侧过身子，从箱子旁边横着走过去
scene: 搬运工没有把柜子直接推向前，而是小心地让它侧向移开。Instead of pulling the cabinet forward, the movers made a lateral shift so that it passed the door frame.
sceneCN: 这里 lateral 是「横向的、侧向的」（第 1 个义项：位于或朝向侧面的方向）；句意：搬运工没有把柜子往前拉，而是做了一个横向移动，让它穿过门框。

derivatives.zh: lateral 加副词后缀 -ly，意为「横向地；从侧面」
lateral 加 -ity 构成名词，指偏侧性、左右不对称性
lateral 加动词后缀 -ize，意为「使侧向化」，常用于大脑功能偏侧化
lateralize 加 -tion，指功能偏向一侧的过程或状态
拉丁语 com + lateralis 构成，原义「同侧的」，引申为间接的、附属的，现在多指抵押担保的

senses.title: Situated at or towards the side
senses.definition: placed at, coming from, or directed towards the side of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物的侧面、从侧面而来或朝向侧面的
senses.example: The doctor examined the lateral view of the injured knee.
senses.exampleCN: 医生查看了受伤膝盖的侧位影像。
senses.why: The Latin root is latus, the side, so the adjective simply says that something belongs to a side.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根是 latus（侧边），所以这个形容词直接表示「属于侧边的」。

senses.title: Sideways instead of forward or back
senses.definition: involving movement or extension sideways, across the usual direction of travel
senses.definitionCN: 涉及横向移动或伸展，穿过通常的前进方向
senses.example: A crab can make a quick lateral movement across the sand.
senses.exampleCN: 螃蟹能在沙滩上快速横向移动。
senses.why: Once side means direction, the word naturally names motion that goes across rather than forwards.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「侧」表示方向，这个词自然指横穿而过的运动，而不是向前。

senses.title: At the same rank or level
senses.definition: at the same level in an organisation, as a move sideways to a post of equal rank
senses.definitionCN: 在组织中处于同一层级，例如平行调动到级别相同的岗位
senses.example: She took a lateral move to a similar position in another department.
senses.exampleCN: 她平调到另一个部门的同级岗位。
senses.why: A change that does not go up or down is pictured as going sideways, so lateral came to mean same-level.
senses.whyCN: 既不上升也不下降的改变被想象成「横着走」，于是 lateral 引申为同级的。

senses.title: Finding ideas along unexpected lines
senses.definition: used of thinking that approaches a problem from an indirect or unexpected angle
senses.definitionCN: 指从旁侧或不寻常角度切入问题的思维方式
senses.example: The puzzle needs a little lateral thinking rather than a longer list.
senses.exampleCN: 这个谜题需要一点横向思维，而不是更长的清单。
senses.why: If the straight path forward is blocked, the mind steps to the side, so indirect problem solving is lateral.
senses.whyCN: 如果向前的直路被挡住，脑子就侧步走；因此间接解题被称为横向思维。

senses.title: Branching off to the side
senses.definition: used of branches, shoots, or roots that grow out to the side of a main stem
senses.definitionCN: 指从主干侧面长出的枝条、芽或根
senses.example: Each lateral branch carries a pair of opposite leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 每根侧枝上长着一对对生的叶子。
senses.why: Botany names a stem that grows from the side, so the lateral branch is the side of the plant made visible.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把从侧面长出的茎称为侧枝，于是「侧」在植物身上变得看得见。

senses.title: The sense-line along a fish or the side part
senses.definition: a line of sense organs along the side of a fish, or a side channel in some organs
senses.definitionCN: 鱼体两侧的感器官线，或某些器官中的侧向管道
senses.example: The lateral line lets a fish feel the movement of water.
senses.exampleCN: 侧线让鱼能感知水的流动。
senses.why: The noun sense keeps the meaning of a side feature, here the side line that carries a special sense.
senses.whyCN: 名词义项保留「侧面之物」的含义，此处的侧线承载着一种特殊感觉。

intro.en: Lateral comes from Latin lateralis, belonging to a side, from latus, the side, through French lateral into English.
intro.cn: lateral 来自拉丁语 lateralis（属于侧面的），源自 latus（侧边），经法语 lateral 进入英语。

items.en: Latus, with stem later-, means the side or flank of a body.
items.cn: latus 的词干为 later-，意为人或物的侧面、胁部。

items.en: Laterum means of the sides, and lateralis means belonging to a side.
items.cn: laterum 意为「侧面的」，lateralis 意为「属于侧面的」。

items.en: Anatomical Latin fixes lateralis for the side of the body, opposite to medialis.
items.cn: 解剖学拉丁语用 lateralis 指身体侧面，与 medialis（内侧的）相对。

items.en: French lateral carries the adjective into general and scientific use.
items.cn: 法语 lateral 把这个形容词带入一般与科学用途。

items.en: English lateral appears in anatomy and geometry before spreading to ordinary speech.
items.cn: 英语 lateral 先出现在解剖学与几何学，随后扩展到日常语言。

items.en: The twentieth century adds lateral thinking and lateral moves in business.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添上「横向思维」与商界的「平调」。

note.en: Lateral belongs to the side family of Latin latus, and stands beside words for sideways, collateral, and bilateral arrangement.
note.cn: lateral 属于拉丁语 latus 的「侧边」词族，并与表示横向、附属、双侧的词相邻。

entries.definition: from or towards the side
the tendency to use one side, especially of the brain
involving two sides
additional or indirect; security for a loan
towards the middle line of the body
entries.definitionCN: 内侧的（与 lateral 相对）

entries.definition: towards or from the side
parallel to the flat ground
slanting rather than straight
on the outer edge

normalIntro.en: Lateral comes from Latin latus, a side, so every meaning of the word stays on one side of something.
normalIntro.cn: lateral 源自拉丁语 latus（侧边），因此这个词的每个义项都停留在某物的某一侧。

normal.en: Compare unilateral and bilateral: one side against two sides, both built on lateral.
normal.cn: 对比 unilateral 与 bilateral：一个是单侧，一个是双侧，两者都由 lateral 构成。

normal.en: A lateral move in a job does not go up or down; it goes to one side.
normal.cn: 工作上的 lateral move 不是升也不是降，而是平着换到一边。

normal.en: Lateral thinking solves a problem by approaching it from an unexpected side.
normal.cn: lateral thinking 从意想不到的侧面切入来解决问题。

normal.en: The lateral line of a fish runs along the side of its body.
normal.cn: 鱼的 lateral line 沿着身体一侧延伸。

normal.en: In anatomy lateral means away from the middle line, so a lateral view is seen from the side.
normal.cn: 在解剖学里 lateral 表示远离中线，所以侧视图是从侧面看到的。

abstract.en: Picture a crab stepping sideways along the sand instead of walking straight.
abstract.cn: 想象一只螃蟹在沙滩上横着走，而不是直着走。

abstract.en: Imagine a box that is too tall for the door until you tilt it onto its long side.
abstract.cn: 想象一只柜子太高进不了门，直到你把它侧过来。

abstract.en: Think of a tree sending out a branch to the left of the trunk.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵树从主干左侧伸出一根枝条。

examples.en: The lateral branch grows at almost right angles to the trunk.
examples.cn: 侧枝几乎与树干成直角生长。

examples.en: Repeated lateral movements can strain the ankle joints.
examples.cn: 反复的横向移动会拉伤踝关节。

examples.en: The report lists lateral links between units as a weak point.
examples.cn: 这份报告把各单位之间的横向联系列为薄弱环节。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「拉的肉」——把肉从一边「拉」到另一边，方向是横着的；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 latus（侧边，词干 later-）→ lateralis（属于侧面的）→ 法语 lateral → 英语 lateral，核心义「在侧边」。

sensesIntro.en: Lateral starts from the plain idea of a side, then spreads to sideways motion, same-level rank, indirect thinking, side branches, and the side line of a fish.
sensesIntro.cn: lateral 从最朴素的「侧边」出发，继而扩展到横向运动、同级职位、间接思维、侧枝以及鱼的侧线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person turning sideways to slip past a cabinet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人侧过身子，从柜子旁边横穿过去。

branches.en: Being at the side is the plain spatial sense.
branches.cn: 位于侧面是最基础的空间义项。

branches.en: Moving sideways is the sense about motion.
branches.cn: 横向移动是关于运动的义项。

branches.en: A same-level move is the organisational sense.
branches.cn: 同级调动是组织领域的义项。

branches.en: Approaching at an angle is the thinking sense.
branches.cn: 斜向切入是思维领域的义项。

branches.en: Side branches, sideways motion, and side lines all make the side visible.
branches.cn: 侧枝、横向运动与侧线都让「侧边」变得可见。

intro.en: Lateral is built on the Latin noun latus and the adjective lateralis, and English thin out around it with laterality, laterally, and collateral.
intro.cn: lateral 建立在拉丁名词 latus 与形容词 lateralis 之上，英语围绕它衍生出 laterality、laterally 与 collateral。

latinIntro.en: Latin latus, with stem later-, means the side, and lateralis means belonging to a side.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 latus（词干 later-）意为侧边，lateralis 意为属于侧面的。

items.example: Latus supplies the side image.
items.exampleCN: latus 提供「侧边」的意象。

items.example: The stem later- builds lateralis.
items.exampleCN: 词干 later- 构成 lateralis。

items.example: Lateralis becomes the French and English adjective.
items.exampleCN: lateralis 演变为法语与英语形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示「与……有关」的形容词后缀

definition_zh: 偏侧性；左右不对称性；单侧优势
definition_en: the tendency to use one side of the body, or one side of the brain, more than the other
core_image: 左手与右手两只手掌并排，一只手明显比另一只更常用
scene: 大脑检查结束后，研究员指着屏幕上的激活区域。The study found clear laterality in the language areas of the brain.
sceneCN: 这里 laterality 是「偏侧性、左右不对称」（第 1 个义项：功能偏向一侧的倾向）；句意：这项研究发现，大脑的语言区存在明显的偏侧性。

pos.zh: 偏侧性；左右不对称性；单侧优势

derivatives.zh: 去掉后缀 -ity 得到的基础形容词，意为「侧面的；横向的」
基础词加动词后缀 -ize，意为「使偏侧化」，指功能集中到一侧
lateralize 加 -ation，指某一功能偏向一侧的过程
前缀 uni- 加 lateral，意为单侧的、一方的

senses.title: The tendency to favour one side of the body
senses.definition: the habit or tendency to use one side of the body, such as the right hand, more than the other
senses.definitionCN: 惯用身体某一侧（如右手）多于另一侧的倾向
senses.example: Tests of laterality showed that most children preferred their right hand.
senses.exampleCN: 偏侧性测试显示大多数儿童都偏好使用右手。
senses.why: The noun is built on lateral, of the side, so laterality names the fact that a body leans toward one side.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由 lateral（侧面的）构成，所以 laterality 指身体偏向一侧这一事实。

senses.title: Functional division between brain sides
senses.definition: the degree to which a function, such as language, is carried out mainly by one side of the brain
senses.definitionCN: 某一功能（如语言）主要由大脑一侧承担的程度
senses.example: Handedness gives only a rough clue to cerebral laterality.
senses.exampleCN: 惯用手只能为大脑偏侧性提供粗略线索。
senses.why: In neurology the side of the brain is the deciding side, so laterality measures how strongly a task is left or right.
senses.whyCN: 在神经学中，大脑的「一侧」是决定性的那一侧，所以 laterality 衡量一项任务偏左或偏右的强度。

senses.title: Left-right asymmetry in an organ
senses.definition: a difference in form or position between the left and right sides of a structure
senses.definitionCN: 身体结构左右两侧在形态或位置上的差异
senses.example: The heart sits with a laterality that is fixed in early development.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏的位置偏侧性在发育早期就已确定。
senses.why: When a single organ is clearly not mirrored, its left and right sides are different, and laterality names that asymmetry.
senses.whyCN: 当某个器官明显不是镜像对称时，它的左右两侧就不一样，laterality 正指这种不对称。

senses.title: A leftward or rightward bias in behaviour
senses.definition: a consistent preference for turning, looking, or acting towards one side
senses.definitionCN: 长期稳定地偏好朝某一侧转动、观看或行动
senses.example: Fish shoals often show a shared laterality when they turn together.
senses.exampleCN: 鱼群集体转向时常常表现出共同的偏侧性。
senses.why: The body-side idea is narrowed again for a habit of animals and people, measured as a bias to one direction.
senses.whyCN: 「身体一侧」的概念再次收窄，用于描述动物与人的习惯，被测量为一个方向上的偏好。

senses.title: Being on one side in medical use
senses.definition: an occasional medical use for the side on which a growth or swelling lies, or for placing something on one side
senses.definitionCN: 偶见于医学术语，指肿块或肿胀所在的那一侧，或指置于侧位
senses.example: The old surgical notes mention a laterality of the tumour.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的外科记录中提到该肿瘤的偏侧位置。
senses.why: In clinical writing the side of a growth must be stated, so the noun carries the sense of being on one side.
senses.whyCN: 在临床书写中必须说明肿块位于哪一侧，因此这个名词承载了「位于一侧」的含义。

intro.en: Laterality is the English noun formed from Latin lateralis, belonging to a side, plus the noun suffix -ity.
intro.cn: laterality 是由拉丁语 lateralis（属于侧面的）加名词后缀 -ity 构成的英语名词。

items.en: Latus, with stem later-, means the side, and lateralis means belonging to a side.
items.cn: latus（词干 later-）意为侧边，lateralis 意为属于侧面的。

items.en: English takes lateral from Latin as an adjective used in anatomy and geometry.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语借入 lateral，作为解剖学与几何学中的形容词。

items.en: The abstract noun suffix -ity is attached, and the word is generally dated to the nineteenth century in English.
items.cn: 加上抽象名词后缀 -ity，该词在英语中的首见时间一般认为在十九世纪。

items.en: Medical writing fixes laterality as the technical word for left-right differences and hemispheric dominance.
items.cn: 医学写作把 laterality 固定为指左右差异与半球优势的技术词。

items.en: Modern psychology and neurology use the term for handedness, brain dominance, and cognitive bias.
items.cn: 现代心理学与神经学用这个词指惯用手、大脑优势与认知偏向。

note.en: Laterality is the abstract noun of the side family, close to lateral, lateralize, and to the paired words handedness and asymmetry.
note.cn: laterality 是「侧边」词族的抽象名词，与 lateral、lateralize 以及成对的 handedness、asymmetry 相邻。

from or towards the side

the process of concentrating a function on one side

normalIntro.en: Laterality is lateral plus the noun ending -ity, so it is the state of having a side that acts more than the other.
normalIntro.cn: laterality 是 lateral 加上名词词尾 -ity，因此指「一侧比另一侧更活跃」的状态。

normal.en: Compare lateral, laterally, and laterality: adjective, adverb, and noun of the same stem.
normal.cn: 对比 lateral、laterally、laterality：同一词干下的形容词、副词与名词。

normal.en: Cerebral laterality describes which half of the brain does a job like language.
normal.cn: cerebral laterality 描述语言等任务由大脑的哪一半承担。

normal.en: Handedness is the everyday measure of laterality.
normal.cn: 惯用手是偏侧性最日常的测量方式。

normal.en: Left laterality and right laterality name the direction that is favoured.
normal.cn: left laterality 与 right laterality 指明所偏好的方向。

normal.en: The verb lateralize and the noun lateralization both mean putting a function onto one side.
normal.cn: 动词 lateralize 与名词 lateralization 都表示把功能放到一侧。

abstract.en: Picture two hands side by side, with one clearly shading the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手并排，其中一只明显盖住了另一只。

abstract.en: Imagine a heart sitting slightly off the middle of the chest.
abstract.cn: 想象心脏略微偏离胸腔正中。

abstract.en: Think of a brain with a bright spot on just one half.
abstract.cn: 想象大脑只有一半亮着。

examples.en: The researchers measured laterality in both the hands and the eyes.
examples.cn: 研究者同时测量了手与眼的偏侧性。

examples.en: Reduced laterality of language is more common in left-handed people.
examples.cn: 语言区偏侧性减弱在左利手中更常见。

examples.en: Tests of laterality help doctors plan the surgery.
examples.cn: 偏侧性测试有助于医生规划手术。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「来特辣乐体」——身体「偏向」一侧，一侧特别「辣」；只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 latus（侧边，词干 later-）→ lateralis（属于侧面的）→ 英语 lateral + 名词后缀 -ity → laterality，核心义「偏向一侧的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Laterality begins as the abstract state of having a side, then settles into handedness, brain dominance, left-right asymmetry, behavioural bias, and an occasional medical use.
sensesIntro.cn: laterality 先泛指「拥有侧边」的抽象状态，随后落地为用手习惯、大脑优势、左右不对称、行为偏向，以及偶尔出现的医学用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands side by side, one of them doing almost all the work.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手并排，其中一只手几乎包揽了全部工作。

branches.en: Preferring one side of the body is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 偏好身体一侧是基础义项。

branches.en: Which brain half does the work is the clinical sense.
branches.cn: 由哪一半大脑承担工作是临床义项。

branches.en: A difference between left and right is the structural sense.
branches.cn: 左右之间的差异是结构义项。

branches.en: A steady shared bias is the behavioural sense.
branches.cn: 稳定的共同偏向是行为义项。

branches.en: Clinical notes record both which half works and where a growth sits.
branches.cn: 临床记录既记工作的一侧，也记肿块所在的一侧。

definition_zh: 赞扬；颂扬；（宗教）歌颂（上帝）
definition_en: to praise someone or something highly, especially in public or in a formal way
core_image: 人群高举的手掌，一起为某人鼓掌叫好
scene: 毕业典礼上，校长念完那位老教师的教龄，全场起立鼓掌。The headmaster stood up to laud the retired teacher for forty years of patient work.
sceneCN: 这里 laud 是「公开赞扬、颂扬」（第 1 个义项：高声称赞某人或某事）；句意：校长起身颂扬这位任教四十年的退休教师的耐心付出。

pos.zh: 赞扬；颂扬（多用于书面与正式场合）
赞美；颂歌（多见于宗教文本与固定短语）

derivatives.zh: 由 laud 加 -able（可……的）构成，义为「值得赞扬的」
由 laudable 加 -ly 构成，义为「值得赞扬地」
由 laud 加 -ation（行为名词后缀）构成，义为「赞美；颂扬」
由 laud 加 -atory（表示性质的形容词后缀）构成，义为「赞美的；颂扬的」
独立成为专名，指天主教「晨祷」，取自颂歌之意

senses.title: To praise someone highly
senses.definition: to speak of a person with strong approval, often in public
senses.definitionCN: 在公开场合高度肯定并称赞某人
senses.example: The mayor lauded the volunteers for their long hours.
senses.exampleCN: 市长盛赞志愿者们长时间工作。
senses.why: The Latin verb laus means praise, and its verb form is simply to give praise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 laus 意为「赞扬」，其动词形式自然就是「给予赞美」。

senses.title: To praise an achievement or quality
senses.definition: to praise a thing such as a work, an effort, or a quality as excellent
senses.definitionCN: 把作品、努力或品质称许为优秀
senses.example: Critics lauded the novel for its honesty.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家称赞这部小说的诚实。
senses.why: The object of praise moved from people to their deeds, so the verb began to take abstract things as objects.
senses.whyCN: 赞扬的对象从人转移到人的事迹，于是这个词开始以抽象事物作宾语。

senses.title: To praise God in worship
senses.definition: to give praise to God or a holy figure in prayer or song
senses.definitionCN: 在祈祷或歌唱中向上帝或神圣人物表达赞美
senses.example: The choir rose to laud the Lord at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班在黎明时起身歌颂主。
senses.why: Medieval Christian services kept the old Latin verb for the highest object of praise, which was God.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪的基督教仪式沿用这个拉丁动词，用在对最高赞美对象——上帝的颂扬上。

intro.en: Laud comes from Latin laus, praise, and its verb laudare, to praise, which passed through Old French into English.
intro.cn: laud 来自拉丁语 laus（赞扬）及其动词 laudare（赞美），经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Laus is the noun for praise, and laudare is to praise.
items.cn: laus 是「赞扬」的名词，laudare 意为「赞美」。

items.en: Church Latin uses laudare chiefly for praising God in the services.
items.cn: 教会拉丁语中 laudare 主要用于在礼仪中赞美上帝。

items.en: Old French loer keeps the meaning, and its noun loenge means praise.
items.cn: 古法语 loer 保留该义，其名词 loenge 意为「赞美」。

items.en: English borrows laud and the related word laudable directly from Latin forms.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语形式借入 laud 与相关词 laudable。

items.en: Laud turns mainly formal and religious, while praise becomes the everyday word.
items.cn: laud 逐渐偏向正式与宗教语境，日常表达让位给 praise。

items.en: Laud survives in written praise and in the fixed name Lauds for morning prayer.
items.cn: laud 保留在书面赞美中，并以专名 Lauds 指晨祷。

note.en: Laud is the formal verb of praise, close to its family laudable, laudatory and lauds, and to ordinary praise words.
note.cn: laud 是正式的「赞扬」动词，与同族的 laudable、laudatory、lauds 相邻，也与普通的赞美词相邻。

entries.definition: deserving praise
expressing praise
the act of praising
making a lot of noise
entries.definitionCN: 大声的；只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to express approval of someone

normalIntro.en: Laud is the short Latin praise verb, and its family shows up in formal and religious English.
normalIntro.cn: laud 是简短的拉丁系「赞美」动词，它的词族多见于正式与宗教语境的英语。

normal.en: Laud someone for something means to praise them for it.
normal.cn: laud someone for something 意为因某事赞扬某人。

normal.en: A widely lauded film is one that many critics have praised.
normal.cn: widely lauded film 指被众多评论家赞许的电影。

normal.en: The related adjective laudable means deserving praise.
normal.cn: 相关形容词 laudable 意为值得赞扬的。

normal.en: Lauds is also the name of the Catholic morning service.
normal.cn: Lauds 也是天主教晨祷的名称。

normal.en: Compare praise: praise is everyday, while laud is formal and slightly bookish.
normal.cn: 对比 praise：praise 更日常，laud 更正式、更书面。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd raising its open palms toward one speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象人群把手掌举向一位说话的人。

abstract.en: Imagine a critic underlining a line of a novel and nodding.
abstract.cn: 想象一位评论家在小说某句下画线，并点头称许。

abstract.en: Picture a choir at dawn singing the old Latin word aloud.
abstract.cn: 想象唱诗班在黎明唱出古老的拉丁词语。

examples.en: The judges lauded her design for its simple, practical lines.
examples.cn: 评委们称赞她的设计线条简洁而实用。

examples.en: His decision to donate the prize money was widely lauded.
examples.cn: 他捐出奖金的决定广获赞誉。

examples.en: In the chronicle, monks laud the founder of the abbey.
examples.cn: 在编年史中，修士们颂扬这座修道院的创建者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劳德」——干得辛苦（劳）又有德，自然值得高声赞扬；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 laus（赞扬）+ 动词后缀 -dare → laudare（赞美）；名词干 laud- 直接进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Laud begins as praise of people, then praise of their works and qualities, and finally praise offered to God.
sensesIntro.cn: laud 先指对人的赞扬，再指对作品与品质的称许，最后指向上帝表达的颂扬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: raised palms giving praise in a public voice.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群中举起的手掌，公开表达赞美。

branches.en: Praising a person in public is the first sense.
branches.cn: 公开赞扬一个人是第一义项。

branches.en: Praise shifts from people to works and qualities.
branches.cn: 赞美对象从人转移到作品与品质。

branches.en: Worship is praise directed at the highest object.
branches.cn: 歌颂是把赞美指向最高的对象。

branches.en: Both the person and the deed can carry the praise.
branches.cn: 人与事迹都可以承载赞美的对象。

branches.en: Public praise and sacred praise share the same raised voice.
branches.cn: 公开的赞美与神圣的颂扬共有同一种高声称许。

intro.en: Laud is a Latin praise noun and verb, with English forms such as lauded, laudable, laudatory, and the fixed name Lauds.
intro.cn: laud 源自拉丁语的「赞扬」名词与动词，英语围绕它构成 lauded、laudable、laudatory 以及专名 Lauds。

latinIntro.en: Latin laus is praise, and laudare is the verb to praise; laudes is the plural for praises.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laus 是「赞扬」，laudare 是动词「赞美」，laudes 是复数「赞歌」。

items.example: Laus gives the noun stem laud-.
items.exampleCN: laus 提供名词词干 laud-。

items.example: Laudare is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: laudare 是英语动词的直接来源。

items.example: The plural laudes names the morning prayer.
items.exampleCN: 复数 laudes 成为晨祷之名。

items.example: Laud is chiefly formal or literary.
items.exampleCN: laud 主要用于正式或文学语境。

items.example: Lauded is common in the press as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: lauded 在新闻中常作形容词使用。

items.example: The suffix -able forms laudable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 laudable。

items.example: Laudable describes a worthy effort.
items.exampleCN: laudable 形容值得称许的努力。

items.example: The suffix -atory forms laudatory.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -atory 构成 laudatory。

items.example: Laudatory reviews are full of praise.
items.exampleCN: laudatory reviews 即满是赞美的评论。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms laudation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 laudation。

items.example: In the tradition Lauds is the first prayer of the day.
items.exampleCN: 传统上晨祷是一天中的第一次祈祷。

definition_zh: 值得赞扬的；可嘉的；令人称许的
definition_en: deserving praise, even if not fully successful or perfect
core_image: 一张盖了好评印章的纸，边角却还有点毛糙
scene: 一个学生把攒下的零花钱全部投进校门口的捐款箱，钱不多，心意却让人点头。Her donation was small but laudable, and the teacher mentioned it in class.
sceneCN: 这里 laudable 是「值得赞扬、可嘉的」（第 1 个义项：某事值得称许，不论成就大小）；句意：她的捐款不多，但值得赞扬，老师在班上提到了这件事。

collocations.phrase: a laudable attempt to do something

derivatives.zh: 由 laudable 加 -ly 构成，义为「值得赞扬地」
由拉丁语 laudare 直接借入的动词，义为「赞扬」（laudable 的基础词）
由 laud 加 -atory 构成，义为「赞美的；颂扬的」，侧重表达方式而非价值判断
由 laudable 加 -ness 构成，义为「值得赞扬之处」
由 laud 加前缀 ill- 构成，义为「受到苛评的」，主要用于文学语境

senses.title: Deserving praise in effort or intention
senses.definition: praiseworthy because the aim or effort is good, whatever the result
senses.definitionCN: 因目标或努力良好而值得称赞，不论结果如何
senses.example: The scheme to plant trees was a laudable effort.
senses.exampleCN: 植树计划是一项可嘉的努力。
senses.why: The suffix -able means worthy of, so laud plus -able is simply worthy of praise.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -able 意为「值得……的」，因此 laud 加 -able 就是「值得赞扬的」。

senses.title: Praiseworthy yet open to a caveat
senses.definition: praiseworthy in principle but often said of hopes that may not work out
senses.definitionCN: 原则上值得称赞，但常用来暗示效果未必理想
senses.example: It is a laudable aim, but the budget is far too small.
senses.exampleCN: 这个目标值得称许，但预算远远不够。
senses.why: Because the word praises intention, English often adds a but to contrast the aim with the outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这个词赞美的是用意，因此英语常用 but 把目标与结果对照起来。

senses.title: Praiseworthy in a formal tribute
senses.definition: used formally to endorse someone as commendable in a speech or record
senses.definitionCN: 在演说或记录中正式肯定某人是值得称许的
senses.example: Her conduct throughout the crisis was entirely laudable.
senses.exampleCN: 她在整个危机中的表现完全值得称许。
senses.why: The Latin adjective laudabilis appears in written recognitions, and that formal tone survives today.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语形容词 laudabilis 用于书面表彰，这种正式语气延续至今。

senses.title: Applied to a quality rather than a deed
senses.definition: used of a personal quality, such as honesty or patience, that earns respect
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容诚实、耐心等值得尊重的个人品质
senses.example: He showed a laudable honesty about his own mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己犯下的错误表现出可嘉的诚实。
senses.why: Praise moved from single acts to the qualities behind them, so the adjective now qualifies habits of character.
senses.whyCN: 赞美从单个行为转到支撑行为的内在品质，因此这个形容词也能修饰品格习惯。

intro.en: Laudable joins Latin laus, praise, with the suffix -abilis, worthy of, giving laudabilis, worthy of praise.
intro.cn: laudable 把拉丁语 laus（赞扬）与后缀 -abilis（值得……的）结合，形成 laudabilis（值得赞扬的）。

items.en: Laudabilis is formed from laudare, to praise, plus the suffix -abilis.
items.cn: laudabilis 由 laudare（赞美）加后缀 -abilis 构成。

items.en: Classical Latin uses laudabilis for things worthy of praise or of note.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语用 laudabilis 指值得赞扬或值得注意的事物。

items.en: Old French loable keeps the adjective, and English later borrows the Latin form directly.
items.cn: 古法语 loable 保留该形容词，英语后来则直接借入拉丁形式。

items.en: Laudable is recorded in Middle English in the sense worthy of praise.
items.cn: laudable 在中古英语中已见记录，义为「值得赞扬的」。

items.en: The adjective spreads into political and moral writing as a formal word of approval.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，这个形容词在政治与道德写作中作为正式褒词扩展使用。

items.en: The word now often praises good intentions while leaving room for criticism.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词常赞美良好用意，同时为保留批评留出余地。

note.en: Laudable is the adjective of worthiness behind laud; it pairs naturally with aim, effort, and intention.
note.cn: laudable 是 laud 词族中表示「值得」的形容词，常与目标、努力、用意等词搭配。

normalIntro.en: Memorize laudable as laud plus the suffix -able, worthy of being praised.
normalIntro.cn: 把 laudable 记成 laud 加后缀 -able，即「值得被赞扬的」。

normal.en: The suffix -able turns praise into worthiness, as in readable and believable.
normal.cn: 后缀 -able 把动作变成「值得」，如 readable 与 believable。

normal.en: Laudable usually sits before aim, effort, or intention, not before results.
normal.cn: laudable 常放在 aim、effort、intention 前，较少修饰结果。

normal.en: A laudable aim followed by but signals a gap between hope and reality.
normal.cn: laudable aim 后接 but 表示希望与现实之间还有差距。

normal.en: The adverb laudably describes how someone acted.
normal.cn: 副词 laudably 描述某人行事的方式。

normal.en: Compare praiseworthy: it is plainer and more common in speech.
normal.cn: 对比 praiseworthy：它更朴素，口语中更常用。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp marked good on a slightly ragged page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张边角有点毛糙的纸盖上了「好评」印章。

abstract.en: Picture a small coin dropping into a charity box.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币落进捐款箱。

abstract.en: Picture a medal handed over for good conduct, not for first prize.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚表彰品行、而非冠军的奖章被递到手中。

examples.en: Trying to save every old building was a laudable aim.
examples.cn: 设法保住每一栋老建筑是一个值得称许的目标。

examples.en: Her efforts to teach adults to read were truly laudable.
examples.cn: 她教成年人识字，努力确实可嘉。

examples.en: The plan was laudable in principle but costly in practice.
examples.cn: 这个计划原则上值得称赞，实践中却代价高昂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劳德博」——辛勤劳动又有品德，值得博得一声称赞；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 laus（赞扬）+ -abilis（值得……的）→ laudabilis（值得赞扬的）→ 英语 laudable。

sensesIntro.en: Laudable praises a good effort, then a good intention with a caveat, then a formal tribute, and finally a personal quality.
sensesIntro.cn: laudable 先赞美良好的努力，再指常带保留的善意初衷，然后指正式表彰，最后指个人品格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a good-mark stamp on a slightly ragged page.
core.cn: 核心意象：边角毛糙的纸上盖了一枚「好评」印章。

branches.en: Praising a good effort is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 赞美良好的努力是最常见的义项。

branches.en: Praise for intention often comes with a caveat.
branches.cn: 对用意的赞美常常附带保留。

branches.en: Formal recognition is praise in a public record or speech.
branches.cn: 正式表彰是在公共记录或演说中的赞美。

branches.en: Praise of a quality extends the word from acts to character.
branches.cn: 对品质的赞美把词从行为扩展到品格。

branches.en: Effort, intention, and quality share the idea of worth rather than success.
branches.cn: 努力、用意与品质都落在「值得」而非「成功」上。

intro.en: Laudable is a Latin-ablaut adjective: the root laud- carries praise and the suffix -able makes it worthy of praise.
intro.cn: laudable 是拉丁词根形容词：词根 laud- 承载「赞扬」，后缀 -able 使之成为「值得赞扬」。

latinIntro.en: Latin laudare means to praise, and laudabilis joins that verb to the suffix -abilis, worthy of.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laudare 意为赞美，laudabilis 把这个动词与后缀 -abilis（值得……的）结合。

items.example: Laudare supplies the root laud-.
items.exampleCN: laudare 提供词根 laud-。

items.meaning: worthy of being, able to be
items.example: The suffix -abilis makes a verb into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -abilis 把动词变成形容词。

items.example: Laudabilis is the direct Latin parent.
items.exampleCN: laudabilis 是直接拉丁语母词。

items.example: Laudable is the borrowed form of laudabilis.
items.exampleCN: laudable 是 laudabilis 的借入形式。

items.example: The suffix -able replaces Latin -abilis.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 取代拉丁语 -abilis。

items.example: Laud is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: laud 是这一词族的基础动词。

items.example: The suffix -ly turns laudable into an adverb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 把 laudable 变为副词 laudably。

items.example: Laudatory shares the same root but a different suffix.
items.exampleCN: laudatory 同根，但后缀不同。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms laudableness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 laudableness。

definition_zh: 月桂树；桂冠；荣誉；桂叶（烹饪调味）
definition_en: an evergreen shrub with glossy leaves, also its leaves as herbs and the crown of victory made from them
core_image: 一顶由光亮绿叶编成的冠，落在胜利者头上
scene: 古希腊的赛场边，观众把刚采下的绿叶编成圆环，等候冠军跑过终点。The victor was crowned with laurel before the crowd could reach him.
sceneCN: 这里 laurel 是「桂冠」（第 4 个义项：由月桂叶编成、象征胜利的冠冕）；句意：人群还来不及靠近，胜者就已经戴上了桂冠。

pos.zh: 月桂树；月桂叶；桂冠；荣誉

collocations.zh: 靠着已有荣誉歇脚、不再努力（习语改写）
提防自己的荣誉被人夺走（习语改写）

derivatives.zh: 由 laurel 的拉丁词干 laure- 加 -ate 构成，义为「荣获桂冠的」
由 laurel 加 -ed 构成，义为「戴上桂冠的；备受赞誉的」
复合词，义为「月桂叶状的」
借自希腊语 Daphne 的植物学名，指月桂属植物

senses.title: The evergreen shrub itself
senses.definition: a shrub with shiny, aromatic leaves that stays green all year
senses.definitionCN: 一种叶片光亮芳香、四季常绿的灌木
senses.example: A tall laurel shades the south wall of the garden.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵高大的月桂树为花园南墙遮阴。
senses.why: The word names the plant first, because that is the thing the Latin noun referred to.
senses.whyCN: 这个词首先指植物本身，因为拉丁语名词最初指的就是这种树。

senses.title: The dried leaf used in cooking
senses.definition: the dried leaves of the shrub, used to flavor soups and stews
senses.definitionCN: 晒干的月桂叶，用于给汤和炖菜调味
senses.example: Add two dried laurel leaves to the stew and simmer.
senses.exampleCN: 往炖菜里加两片干月桂叶，小火慢炖。
senses.why: Part of a plant easily stands for the plant, so the leaf became a kitchen word in its own right.
senses.whyCN: 植物的部分可以代指整体，于是叶子独立成为烹饪用词。

senses.title: The wreath woven from its leaves
senses.definition: a circular wreath made of laurel branches
senses.definitionCN: 用月桂枝叶编成的圆环形花冠
senses.example: The winner wore a wreath of laurel on the field.
senses.exampleCN: 获胜者在赛场上戴着月桂花冠。
senses.why: The Greek and Roman winners were crowned with laurel, so the woven object took the plants name.
senses.whyCN: 古希腊罗马的优胜者以月桂加冕，于是编成的花冠借用了植物之名。

senses.title: The crown of victory
senses.definition: a symbol of victory, honor, or supreme achievement
senses.definitionCN: 胜利、荣誉或最高成就的象征
senses.example: Election night brought him the laurel he had chased for years.
senses.exampleCN: 选举之夜为他带来了追逐多年的桂冠。
senses.why: Because the wreath marked a winner, the word shifted from the object to the victory it stands for.
senses.whyCN: 花冠是胜利者的标志，词义便从物品转向它所象征的胜利。

senses.title: Honor and distinction
senses.definition: honor, fame, or distinction gained through success
senses.definitionCN: 因成功而获得的荣誉、名声或显赫地位
senses.example: The old poet never sought laurel, only a quiet room.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老诗人从不追求荣誉，只求一间安静的屋子。
senses.why: Once victory became abstract, the word could name honor itself rather than any object.
senses.whyCN: 胜利一旦抽象化，这个词就能直接指荣誉本身，而不指具体物件。

intro.en: English laurel goes back through Old French to Latin laurus, the laurel tree, which also gives laureate.
intro.cn: 英语 laurel 经古法语上溯到拉丁语 laurus（月桂树），laureate 也出自同一词根。

items.en: The ultimate origin of the name is uncertain; a pre-Greek Mediterranean source is often assumed.
items.cn: 这个词的最终来源不确定，一般认为来自前希腊时期地中海地区的底源词。

items.en: Greek daphne and Latin laurus are linked in the story of Apollo and Daphne.
items.cn: 希腊语 daphne 与拉丁语 laurus 在阿波罗与达芙妮的神话中被联系起来。

items.en: Laurus is the laurel tree, and laurea means the laurel wreath.
items.cn: laurus 指月桂树，laurea 指月桂花冠。

items.en: Old French lorier, the laurel tree, is the immediate source of the English noun.
items.cn: 古法语 lorier（月桂树）是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Laurel enters English in the sense of the tree and its wreath.
items.cn: laurel 在十四世纪进入英语，义为月桂树及其编成的花冠。

items.en: The wreath sense spreads into honor and fame, and the surname and place name Laurel are separate words.
items.cn: 花冠义向荣誉与名声扩展；人名与地名的 Laurel 则是另外的来源。

note.en: Laurel is the tree, its leaf, and the crown of honor; its family circles laureate, while similar words bring in other victory symbols.
note.cn: laurel 同时指树、叶与荣誉之冠；同族词围绕 laureate，近义词则带出其他胜利象征。

entries.definitionCN: 化学中的「月桂基」；只是拼写与读音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a circle of flowers or leaves

normalIntro.en: It helps to think of laurel as one leaf standing for four things: tree, leaf, crown, and honor.
normalIntro.cn: 把 laurel 想成一片叶子代表四样东西：树、叶、冠、誉。

normal.en: Bay laurel is the culinary name of the tree, so bay leaf and laurel are the same herb.
normal.cn: bay laurel 是这种树的烹饪名称，因此 bay leaf 与 laurel 是同一调味叶。

normal.en: A laurel wreath is the crown of a winner, from the Greek games.
normal.cn: laurel wreath 即胜利者的冠，源于希腊竞技。

normal.en: The idiom for laziness after success is built around laurels, the plural honors.
normal.cn: 表示功成名就后不再努力的习语，正是用复数 laurels（荣誉）构成的。

normal.en: Laureate means crowned with laurel, so a poet laureate is a national poet of honor.
normal.cn: laureate 意为戴桂冠，因此 poet laureate 指一国的荣誉诗人。

normal.en: Compare wreath and garland: both are woven circles, but only laurel insists on honor.
normal.cn: 对比 wreath 与 garland：两者都是编成的圆环，只有 laurel 强调荣誉。

abstract.en: Picture dark glossy leaves knotted into a circle.
abstract.cn: 想象墨绿光亮的叶子被编成一个圆环。

abstract.en: Picture a pot of soup with one broad leaf floating on top.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅汤上浮着一片宽大的叶子。

abstract.en: Picture a runner slowing down at the finish line.
abstract.cn: 想象赛跑者在终点线放慢脚步。

examples.en: A clipped laurel hedge runs along the front path.
examples.cn: 修剪整齐的月桂树篱沿着前院的步道延伸。

examples.en: The cook dropped a dried laurel into the stew.
examples.cn: 厨师把一片干月桂叶放进炖菜里。

examples.en: No laurel was enough for the squad after their defeat.
examples.cn: 球队落败之后，任何荣誉都无济于事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老肉了」——炖老肉要放香叶，香叶就是月桂叶；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 laurus（月桂树）→ 古法语 lorier → 英语 laurel；同根词 laureate 取自同一词干 laure-。

sensesIntro.en: Laurel starts as a plant, then its leaf, then the wreath, the victory, and finally honor itself.
sensesIntro.cn: laurel 从植物起头，再指叶子、花冠、胜利，最后落到荣誉本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ring of glossy green leaves placed on a victors head.
core.cn: 核心意象：一顶光亮绿叶编成的冠，戴在胜利者头上。

branches.en: The plant is the oldest and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 植物是最古老、最字面的义项。

branches.en: The leaf is the plant seen as food.
branches.cn: 叶子是作为食物的那部分植物。

branches.en: The wreath and the victory are one symbol seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 花冠与胜利是同一象征的两个侧面。

branches.en: Victory passes into honor once the object is forgotten.
branches.cn: 当实物被淡忘，胜利便转化为荣誉。

branches.en: The evergreen plant and the crown share the same leaf.
branches.cn: 常绿植物与桂冠共用同一片叶子。

intro.en: Laurel itself is a borrowed noun from Latin laurus; the family adds -ate, -ed, and compounds such as laurel leaf.
intro.cn: laurel 本身是从拉丁语 laurus 借入的名词，词族由此加 -ate、-ed 以及复合形式构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin laurus is the laurel tree and laurea is the laurel wreath; the stem laure- gives English laureate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laurus 是月桂树，laurea 是桂冠；词干 laure- 生成英语 laureate。

items.example: Laurus is the base noun of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: laurus 是整个词族的基础名词。

items.example: Laurea names the wreath of victory.
items.exampleCN: laurea 指胜利的桂冠。

items.example: The Old French form is the immediate source of laurel.
items.exampleCN: 古法语形式是 laurel 的直接来源。

items.example: Laurel carries plant and symbol at once.
items.exampleCN: laurel 同时承载植物与象征。

items.example: Laurels in the plural often means honors.
items.exampleCN: 复数 laurels 常指荣誉。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms laureate.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成 laureate。

items.example: Laureate is used in poet laureate.
items.exampleCN: laureate 见于 poet laureate。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms laurelled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 laurelled。

items.example: Bay leaf is the everyday kitchen name.
items.exampleCN: bay leaf 是日常烹饪中的叫法。

definition_zh: 奢侈的；过分慷慨的；丰富的；慷慨地给予；挥霍
definition_en: giving or spending very generously, often more than is needed, or existing in large amounts
core_image: 宴席上酒水像下雨一样往杯子里倒，桌边的果盘堆得满出来
scene: 婚宴上主人把一只只银盘端上来，水果和甜点堆得满出来。The host put on a lavish wedding and invited three hundred guests.
sceneCN: 这里 lavish 是「豪华的、铺张的」（第 1 个义项：花得极多、极其奢侈的）；句意：主人办了一场铺张的婚礼，邀请了三百位客人。

pos.zh: 奢侈的；过分慷慨的；丰富的

derivatives.zh: 由 lavishly 加副词后缀构成，义为「奢侈地；慷慨地；极其」
由 lavishly 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「奢华；铺张」
由 un- 加 lavish 构成，义为「不铺张的；朴素的」

senses.title: Costing a great deal
senses.definition: costing or spending much more than is usual or necessary
senses.definitionCN: 花费远超平常或超出必要的
senses.example: They stayed in a lavish hotel with marble floors and a private pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住进一家豪华酒店，铺着大理石地板，还有一个私人泳池。
senses.why: Old French lavasse meant a downpour, an image of something poured out without measure, and the adjective took that overflowing sense.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 lavasse 意为暴雨，意象是毫无节制地倾倒，这个形容词承袭的就是这种「满溢」的感觉。

senses.title: Very generous with money or things
senses.definition: giving money, gifts, or help in very large amounts
senses.definitionCN: 给钱、送礼或帮忙都极为大方的
senses.example: Her grandparents were lavish with presents at every birthday.
senses.exampleCN: 她的祖父母每逢生日都送一大堆礼物。
senses.why: The same overflow that describes expensive things also describes an open hand that gives far more than expected.
senses.whyCN: 描述昂贵之物的那种「溢出」，同样可以描述一只远超预期、大方给物的手。

senses.title: Existing in large amounts
senses.definition: existing or supplied in large, almost excessive quantities
senses.definitionCN: 数量大得近乎过分的
senses.example: The report was illustrated with lavish detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告配有大量细致的插图。
senses.why: From money and food the idea of plenty spreads to anything supplied in excess, such as detail or attention.
senses.whyCN: 从金钱与食物出发，「丰盛」的观念扩展到任何给得过多的东西，比如细节或关注。

senses.title: To give generously
senses.definition: to give or spend something in large and generous amounts, often as a verb with on or upon
senses.definitionCN: 以大量且慷慨的方式给予或花费，作动词时多与 on 或 upon 连用
senses.example: The coach lavished praise on the young goalkeeper.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对这个年轻守门员大加赞扬。
senses.why: In modern use the adjective turned into a verb, and to lavish is simply to pour something out on someone.
senses.whyCN: 现代英语里这个形容词转化为动词，lavish 就是把某物倾泻到某人身上。

senses.title: To spend wastefully
senses.definition: to use one large sum after another without care for the cost
senses.definitionCN: 一笔接一笔地花钱而不顾花费
senses.example: He lavished his entire inheritance on a string of parties.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整份遗产挥霍在一场又一场的派对上。
senses.why: When giving becomes reckless, the same overflowing image turns negative and the verb means to squander.
senses.whyCN: 当给予变得不顾后果，同样的满溢意象就转为负面，动词便意为挥霍。

senses.title: Too rich for everyday taste
senses.definition: decorated so richly that it seems showy or in poor taste
senses.definitionCN: 装饰得过于华丽而显得招摇或俗气的
senses.example: Critics found the film a lavish but shallow spectacle.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家认为这部电影场面华丽却内容空洞。
senses.why: The downpour image can flood a style as well as a purse, so lavishness in design slides from rich into gaudy.
senses.whyCN: 暴雨的意象既能淹没钱包也能淹没风格，所以在设计上奢华会滑向俗艳。

intro.en: Lavish comes from Old French lavasse, a downpour of rain, built on the Latin verb lavare, to wash.
intro.cn: lavish 来自古法语 lavasse（暴雨），由拉丁语动词 lavare（冲洗）构成。

items.en: Lavare means to wash or bathe, with no idea of money at first.
items.cn: lavare 意为冲洗或洗浴，起初与金钱毫无关系。

items.en: A related form in medieval use grew into words for a sudden heavy rain.
items.cn: 与之相关的中世纪形式发展出表示骤降大雨的词。

items.en: Lavasse means a downpour or a great flood of rain.
items.cn: lavasse 意为瓢泼大雨或滔天雨洪。

items.en: The noun lavish first names profusion in English, meaning extravagant plenty.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语先出现名词 lavish，指「过量、丰盛」。

items.en: The adjective lavishing and later lavish describe generous or excessive spending, and a verb follows.
items.cn: 后来的形容词 lavishing 与 lavish 描述慷慨或过度的花费，随后又有了动词用法。

items.en: Today lavish covers money, praise, detail, and design, always with a sense of overflow.
items.cn: 今天的 lavish 覆盖金钱、赞扬、细节与设计，始终带着「满溢」的意味。

note.en: Lavish stands beside its own family and near words for extravagant, abundant, and overwhelming generosity.
note.cn: lavish 与自己的词族并列，并与表示奢侈、丰盛和慷慨过头的词相邻。

entries.definition: in a very generous or expensive way
the quality of being very generous or costly
a room with a sink and a toilet
entries.definitionCN: 洗手间；厕所，与 lavish 同出拉丁语 lavare（冲洗），是同源词

entries.definition: spending much more than one can afford
willing to give much of what one has
showily rich and full of costly things

normalIntro.en: Lavish is an overflowing word: money, food, and praise are poured out faster than they can be used.
normalIntro.cn: lavish 是一个「满溢」的词：钱、食物和赞扬都被倒得又急又多，根本用不完。

normal.en: Lavish comes from a word for a downpour, so it pictures things coming down in a flood.
normal.cn: lavish 来自表示「暴雨」的词，所以它画面里的东西是倾泻而下的。

normal.en: Use lavish as an adjective before a noun: a lavish meal, a lavish party, a lavish hotel.
normal.cn: lavish 作形容词放在名词前：a lavish meal、a lavish party、a lavish hotel。

normal.en: Use lavish as a verb with on: to lavish praise on somebody.
normal.cn: lavish 作动词时与 on 搭配：to lavish praise on somebody。

normal.en: The adverbs and nouns are lavishly, lavishness, and unlavish.
normal.cn: 它的副词与名词形式是 lavishly、lavishness 与 unlavish。

normal.en: Compare generous: generous is praise for a kind giver, while lavish hints that the giving is over the top.
normal.cn: 对比 generous：generous 是对善良给予者的称赞，lavish 则暗示给得有些过头。

abstract.en: Picture a banquet table where fruit is piled higher than the plates.
abstract.cn: 想象一张宴席桌，水果堆得比盘子还高。

abstract.en: Imagine rain pouring onto a garden for hours without stopping.
abstract.cn: 想象雨水在花园上倾泻了好几个小时，一刻不停。

abstract.en: See a hand shaking more coins out of a purse than anyone could hold.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从钱袋里倒出的硬币多到没人拿得住。

examples.en: The museum opened with a lavish display of gold and ivory.
examples.cn: 博物馆以一场金与象牙的奢华展览开幕。

examples.en: She was lavished with attention after her first novel appeared.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说问世后，受到了极大的关注。

examples.en: Even a modest salary can feel lavish after months of living on bread and tea.
examples.cn: 吃了几个月的面包和茶之后，哪怕一份微薄的薪水也显得阔绰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉威士」——一边「拉」来一边「威」风，花钱大方到像倒雨水；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 lavare（冲洗、倾注）→ 古法语 lavasse（暴雨、倾泻）→ 英语 lavish（丰盛；豪奢）→ 形容词「铺张的」、动词「慷慨给予」；核心义「像雨一样倒不完」。

sensesIntro.en: Lavish begins with costly things, moves to open-handed giving and abundant supply, then to the verb of giving or squandering, and finally to style that seems showy.
sensesIntro.cn: lavish 从昂贵的东西开始，转向大方给予与大量供应，再转为表示给予或挥霍的动词，最后指过分华丽、显摆的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: wine poured like rain until the cup overflows.
core.cn: 核心意象：酒像雨一样倒下来，杯子满得溢出去。

branches.en: Overflow turns into a high price tag for hotels, meals, and gifts.
branches.cn: 溢出的感觉变成酒店、餐食与礼物上的高价。

branches.en: The same overflow belongs to a generous giver.
branches.cn: 同样的溢出属于一位慷慨的给予者。

branches.en: Plenty in things and plenty in act share one image.
branches.cn: 物的丰盛与行为的慷慨共用一个意象。

branches.en: When the pouring has no stop, generosity becomes waste.
branches.cn: 倾泻不止时，慷慨就变成了挥霍。

branches.en: An overflowing style looks showy as much as rich.
branches.cn: 溢出的风格既显得富丽，也显得招摇。

intro.en: Lavish is built on the Latin washing verb lavare and reached English through a French word for heavy rain.
intro.cn: lavish 建立在拉丁语表示「冲洗」的动词 lavare 之上，经由法语中表示大雨的词进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin lavare means to wash, and its family includes lavatio, a washing or bath.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lavare 意为「冲洗」，其词族包括 lavatio（洗涤、洗浴）。

items.example: Lavare supplies the image of water poured out.
items.exampleCN: lavare 提供水被倾倒而出的意象。

items.example: Lavatio shows the washing family in Latin.
items.exampleCN: lavatio 展示了拉丁语中「洗」的词族。

items.example: Lavasse is the French link that turns washing into pouring.
items.exampleCN: lavasse 是把「洗」变成「倾泻」的法语一环。

items.example: Lavish describes things given or spent without measure.
items.exampleCN: lavish 形容给予或花费毫无节制。

items.meaning: to give or spend very generously
items.example: The verb takes on or upon after it.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词后面接 on 或 upon。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms lavishly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 lavishly。

items.example: Lavishly describes how money or praise is given.
items.exampleCN: lavishly 描述金钱或赞扬被给予的方式。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质的抽象名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms lavishness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 lavishness。

items.example: Lavishness names the quality rather than the thing.
items.exampleCN: lavishness 指这种性质而不是具体事物。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unlavish.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unlavish。

definition_zh: 合法的；法定的；守法的；正当的
definition_en: allowed or required by law, or living and acting according to the law
core_image: 法官把一枚刻着法条的印章稳稳盖在文件上，印章落处即为许可
scene: 移民官员检查完文件，把印章盖在护照上，示意她可以留下。After a long check, the officer agreed the visa was lawful.
sceneCN: 这里 lawful 是「合法的、符合规定的」（第 1 个义项：依据法律被允许、不违反法律）；句意：经过长时间的检查，官员承认这张签证是合法的。

pos.zh: 合法的；法定的；守法的；正当的

derivatives.zh: 由 lawful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「合法地；依法」
由 lawful 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「合法性」
由 un- 加 lawful 构成，义为「非法的；违法的」
由 law 加后缀 -less 构成，义为「无法无天的；不守法律的」

senses.title: Permitted by law
senses.definition: allowed by the law and not breaking it
senses.definitionCN: 被法律允许且不违反法律的
senses.example: It is lawful to record your own phone calls.
senses.exampleCN: 录下自己的电话通话是合法的。
senses.why: Law comes from a root for what is laid down or established, and the suffix -ful means full of it, so lawful is full of established law.
senses.whyCN: law 的本义「被立下、被确立之事」，后缀 -ful 表示「充满」，所以 lawful 就是「充满既定法度的」。

senses.title: Allowed under the rules in force
senses.definition: done in the correct official way, so that it is recognised as valid
senses.definitionCN: 以正确的官方程序完成、因而被承认有效的
senses.example: The officer asked whether the permit was lawful.
senses.exampleCN: 官员询问这张许可证是否符合规定。
senses.why: In official settings the law is more than the statute book: the rules of an office also decide what is lawful.
senses.whyCN: 在公务场景里，「法」不只是一本法典，一个机构的规章同样决定什么算 lawful。

senses.title: Required by law
senses.definition: fixed or demanded by law, so that people must follow it
senses.definitionCN: 由法律固定或要求、人们必须遵从的
senses.example: The lawful minimum wage rose again this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的法定最低工资再次上调。
senses.why: The same word that marks something allowed also marks something imposed, because a rule both permits and commands.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词既能标出「允许」，也能标出「强制」，因为一条规则既许可又要求。

senses.title: Rightfully belonging to someone
senses.definition: having a proper right to something under the law, especially of ownership
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上对某物享有正当权利的，尤指所有权
senses.example: The cottage passed to its lawful heir after the will was read.
senses.exampleCN: 宣读遗嘱后，小屋归了它的合法继承人。
senses.why: Law decides who may claim, so lawful also means that a claim is properly held and cannot be disputed.
senses.whyCN: 法律决定谁可以主张，所以 lawful 也可以表示一项主张是正当持有、无可争议的。

senses.title: Obeying the law
senses.definition: living an honest life and obeying the law of the land
senses.definitionCN: 诚实生活、遵守国法的
senses.example: Most of the tenants were lawful citizens who simply fell behind.
senses.exampleCN: 大多数房客都是守法的公民，只是拖欠了房租。
senses.why: The full-of-law image moves from actions to people: a person is lawful when law fills the way that person lives.
senses.whyCN: 「充满法度」的意象从行为转到人身上：当一个人生活中充满守法之道，这个人就是 lawful。

senses.title: Fair and just
senses.definition: reasonable and morally right, used of a claim or a purpose that a fair judge would accept
senses.definitionCN: 合理而符合道义的，指连公正的裁判也会认可的诉求或目的
senses.example: Losing a job is a lawful reason to ask for more time.
senses.exampleCN: 失业是申请延期的正当理由。
senses.why: Because a fair law is also just, lawful has long carried a second layer meaning reasonable and morally acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 因为公正的法律同时也是「理」，lawful 很早便带上了「合理、在道义上说得过去」的第二层意思。

intro.en: Lawful is law plus the suffix -ful, and law goes back to Old Norse lag, something laid down.
intro.cn: lawful 由 law 加后缀 -ful 构成，而 law 可追溯到古诺尔斯语 lag（被放定之事）。

items.en: A reconstructed root often given as lagam means something laid or placed down.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构形式 lagam，意为被放下、被安放的东西。

items.en: Lag means a layer or a thing laid down, and by extension the custom laid down for a community.
items.cn: lag 意为层、放定之物，引申为为一个社群立下的习俗规矩。

items.en: The native word laqu comes from the same source and already names a rule.
items.cn: 本土形式 laqu 出自同一来源，已经表示「规条」。

items.en: Lawg and then lawe replace the older forms and settle on the spelling law.
items.cn: lawg 与后来的 lawe 取代更早的形式，最后定为拼写 law。

items.en: The suffix -ful is added to law, and lawful first means possessing the law.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 加到 law 上，lawful 最初意为「拥有法度的」。

items.en: Lawful narrows to what the law permits or requires, and is joined by unlawful and lawfully.
items.cn: lawful 收窄为法律允许或要求之事，并衍生出 unlawful 与 lawfully。

note.en: Lawful pairs with its negatives unlawful and lawless, and stands near legal, legitimate, and licit.
note.cn: lawful 与否定形式 unlawful、lawless 相配，并与 legal、legitimate、licit 相邻。

entries.definition: not allowed by law; illegal
in a way that the law allows
not obeying any law
entries.definitionCN: 无法无天的；不守法律的

entries.definition: allowed by the law, or connected with it
correct according to law or accepted rules
allowed by law or custom

normalIntro.en: Lawful is law plus full: a person or act is lawful when it is full of what the law allows.
normalIntro.cn: lawful 就是 law 加 full：当一个人或一件事充满法律所允许的内容，它就是 lawful。

normal.en: Strip -ful from lawful and you get law, the rule that decides whether something is allowed.
normal.cn: 去掉 lawful 中的 -ful 就得到 law，即决定某事是否被允许的规则。

normal.en: The -ful suffix marks a full tank: lawful means full of law and therefore allowed.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ful 表示「装满」，lawful 就是装满法律、因而是被允许的。

normal.en: Unlawful is the negation, lawfully the adverb, and lawfulness the quality.
normal.cn: unlawful 是否定形式，lawfully 是副词，lawfulness 指这种性质。

normal.en: Do not confuse lawful with lawless: one obeys the law, the other has no law at all.
normal.cn: 不要把 lawful 与 lawless 弄混：前者守法，后者根本无法无天。

normal.en: Compare legal: legal covers law in general, lawful stresses that a rule permits the act.
normal.cn: 对比 legal：legal 泛指与法律有关，lawful 强调规则对该行为予以许可。

abstract.en: Picture a judge stamping a seal that turns any paper into an allowed document.
abstract.cn: 想象一位法官盖章，印章一落，任何纸张都变成获准的文件。

abstract.en: See a road with painted lanes, where every car stays inside the lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一条画着车道的路，每辆车都在线内行驶。

abstract.en: Imagine a door that opens only when a rule card touches the lock.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有拿规则卡片贴上门锁才会打开。

examples.en: The protest was loud but perfectly lawful.
examples.cn: 这场抗议声势很大，但完全合法。

examples.en: Police may enter only if they act in a lawful manner.
examples.cn: 警察只有在依法行事的情况下才能进入。

examples.en: Lawfully owned land can be sold at any time.
examples.cn: 合法拥有的土地随时可以出售。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「劳弗」——老实「劳」动的人，凡事都顺着法律、不敢越界；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺尔斯语 lag（放定之物、层）→ 古英语 laqu（规条）→ 中古英语 law（法律）+ -ful（充满……的）→ lawful；核心义「做事与规矩严丝合缝」。

sensesIntro.en: Lawful moves from allowed by law, to valid under official rules, then to required by law, to rightfully owned, to a person who obeys the law, and finally to what is fair.
sensesIntro.cn: lawful 从法律允许，到符合官方规定、再由法律强制，到所享有的正当权利，再到守法的人，最后指合乎情理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seal pressed on a paper until the stamped mark is clear.
core.cn: 核心意象：印章压上纸张，印痕清清楚楚。

branches.en: The basic sense is what the law allows.
branches.cn: 最基本的义项是法律所允许的。

branches.en: Official rules both recognise and demand the act.
branches.cn: 官方规则既承认这项行为，也要求这项行为。

branches.en: Ownership under law gives a claim to someone.
branches.cn: 依法拥有的所有权使人获得正当主张。

branches.en: The full-of-law image turns from acts to a whole person.
branches.cn: 「充满法度」的意象从行为转到整个人身上。

branches.en: A fair law lets lawful also mean reasonable and just.
branches.cn: 公正的法律使 lawful 也可以表示合理、正当。

intro.en: Lawful is the root law with the Old English suffix -ful, and it stands beside unlawful, lawfully, and lawless.
intro.cn: lawful 是词根 law 加古英语后缀 -ful，周围有 unlawful、lawfully 与 lawless。

latinIntro.en: The modern legal vocabulary uses Latin lex and ius, though law itself is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 现代法律词汇多用拉丁语 lex 与 ius，而 law 本身出自日耳曼语。

items.meaning: a rule made and enforced by authority
items.example: Law is the base of lawful.
items.exampleCN: law 是 lawful 的词根。

items.example: The suffix -ful turns law into lawful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 把 law 变成 lawful。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms lawfully.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 lawfully。

items.example: Lawfully marks how an act is done.
items.exampleCN: lawfully 说明行为是以何种方式完成的。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质的抽象名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms lawfulness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 lawfulness。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unlawful.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unlawful。

items.example: Unlawful is the formal opposite of lawful.
items.exampleCN: unlawful 是 lawful 的正式反义词。

items.example: The suffix -less forms lawless.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -less 构成 lawless。

items.example: Lawless describes a place or a person beyond any rule.
items.exampleCN: lawless 形容超出任何规则的地方或人。

items.example: Lawmaker keeps the base word in a compound.
items.exampleCN: lawmaker 是保留词根的复合词。

definition_zh: 松弛的；不严格的；马虎的；松散的；不严谨的
definition_en: not strict or careful enough, or not tight, firm, or clearly defined
core_image: 一根被拉到极限后又慢慢松回去的橡皮筋，松松垮垮地垂着
scene: 考场里监考老师坐在角落看手机，没人核对证件，交头接耳也没人管。The new manager was known for his lax approach to deadlines.
sceneCN: 这里 lax 是「不严格的、松弛的」（第 1 个义项：管束松、要求不严）；句意：这位新经理以对截止日期要求松懈而出名。

pos.zh: 松弛的；不严格的；马虎的；松散的；不严谨的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语词干加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「松懈；松弛」
由 lax 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「松弛；不严谨」
源自同一拉丁词干 laxare（放松），本义「使松弛之物」，今指「泻药」
由 lax 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「松弛地；不严格地」

senses.title: Not strict about rules
senses.definition: not strict in enforcing rules or in demanding proper behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 执行规则不严、对行为要求不高的
senses.example: Critics blamed lax supervision for the factory accident.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把工厂事故归咎于监管松懈。
senses.why: Latin laxus means loose or slack, and a rule held loosely is a rule not enforced, so lax becomes the word for slack discipline.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 laxus 意为松散、松弛，一条被松松握着的规则就是没被执行的规则，于是 lax 成了「纪律松懈」之说。

senses.title: Careless or not thorough
senses.definition: not careful or thorough, so that mistakes and gaps go unnoticed
senses.definitionCN: 不仔细、不彻底，以致错误与漏洞被忽略
senses.example: A lax proofreader let three typos slip into print.
senses.exampleCN: 一位马虎的校对让三处错字印了出来。
senses.why: When attention is held loosely, detail slips through, and the loosening spreads from rules to the person doing the work.
senses.whyCN: 注意力放松时细节就会漏掉，这种松懈便从规章制度扩散到做事的人身上。

senses.title: Not firm or tight
senses.definition: physically loose, not tightly held, pulled, or fastened
senses.definitionCN: 在物理上松散，没有被握紧、拉紧或系紧
senses.example: The rope hung lax between the two posts.
senses.exampleCN: 绳子松松地垂在两根柱子之间。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: anything that has lost its tension is lax, and the abstract senses all grow out of this slackness.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：任何失去张力的东西都是 lax，所有抽象义项都由这种松弛生长出来。

senses.title: Loose in structure
senses.definition: loosely organised or loosely worded, without a tight structure
senses.definitionCN: 组织松散或措辞松弛、缺少严密结构的
senses.example: The essay had a lax argument that jumped between topics.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文论证松散，话题跳来跳去。
senses.why: A loose rope and a loose argument look alike: neither holds its shape, so lax describes writing and plans too.
senses.whyCN: 松了的绳子和松散的论证看起来一样，都保持不住形状，所以 lax 也可形容文字与计划。

senses.title: Lax in medical use
senses.definition: technically, slack or loose, used of muscles and of loose stools
senses.definitionCN: 在专业用法中指松弛、不紧，用于肌肉以及稀松的粪便
senses.example: The nurse noted that the muscles of the jaw were lax.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录下颌的肌肉是松弛的。
senses.why: Medicine keeps the Latin sense in which any tissue that loses its tone is lax, and the laxative noun comes from the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 医学保留了拉丁语中组织失去张力即为松弛的说法，而名词 laxative 也出自同一个动词。

intro.en: Lax comes straight from Latin laxus, loose or slack, and its verb laxare, to loosen.
intro.cn: lax 直接来自拉丁语 laxus（松散、松弛）及其动词 laxare（放松）。

items.en: A reconstructed root is often written as slag-, meaning slack or loose, though its exact shape is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为有一个重构词根 slag-（松弛、松散），不过其确切形式仍有争论。

items.en: Laxus means loose or slack, and laxare means to loosen or release tension.
items.cn: laxus 意为松散、松弛，laxare 意为放松或解开张力。

items.en: Laxitas names slackness, and laxativus describes what loosens the body.
items.cn: laxitas 指松弛，laxativus 形容能使身体松弛之物。

items.en: Lax enters English through Latin as a word for things not tightly bound.
items.cn: lax 在十四世纪经拉丁语进入英语，表示未被紧紧束缚之物。

items.en: The word spreads to conduct and rules, so that a lax person is careless or undisciplined.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到行为与规章，于是 a lax person 指马虎、缺乏自律的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical, administrative, and linguistic senses side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语把物理、管理与语言三个层面的义项并行保留下来。

note.en: Lax pairs with laxity and laxer, and stands near slack, lenient, and careless.
note.cn: lax 与 laxity、laxer 相配，并与 slack、lenient、careless 相邻。

entries.definition: a lack of strictness or care
a medicine that loosens the bowels
money demanded by a government
entries.definitionCN: 税；税款，只是与 lax 拼写结尾相近，词源不同

entries.definition: not pulled tight, or not busy and careful
not strict in punishing people
not paying enough attention

normalIntro.en: Lax is the shortest word for slack: a rubber band that has lost its pull and hangs loose.
normalIntro.cn: lax 是表示「松」最短的词：一根失去拉力、松松垂着的橡皮筋。

normal.en: Three letters only: l, a, x, all soft and loose, like a band no longer stretched.
normal.cn: 只有三个字母 l、a、x，发音都松，像一根不再被拉紧的带子。

normal.en: The noun is laxity, and -ity marks the quality of being lax.
normal.cn: 名词是 laxity，后缀 -ity 表示这种性质。

normal.en: The same Latin stem gives laxative, a medicine that loosens the body.
normal.cn: 同一拉丁词干还生出 laxative，即让身体「松」下来的泻药。

normal.en: Say be lax about rules or lax on security to show what is being handled too loosely.
normal.cn: 用 be lax about 或 lax on 来表明哪方面被处置得太松。

normal.en: Compare lenient: a lenient judge softens the punishment, while a lax rule is simply not enforced.
normal.cn: 对比 lenient：宽大的法官减轻惩罚，而 lax 的规则干脆没人执行。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber band that snaps back and lies flat on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡皮筋弹回来，软软地摊在桌上。

abstract.en: See a door on a broken hinge swinging open a little in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇坏了的门，在风里松松地晃开一点。

abstract.en: Imagine a net with wide holes letting fish swim straight through.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网眼大大的网，鱼成群地直接穿过去。

examples.en: The school was criticised for its lax rules on mobile phones.
examples.cn: 这所学校因对手机的规定松散而受到批评。

examples.en: Lax hiring checks allowed the false certificate to pass unnoticed.
examples.cn: 马虎的招聘审查让那张假证书蒙混过关。

examples.en: Laxity in the laboratory was blamed for the ruined samples.
examples.cn: 实验室的松懈被指为样品损毁的原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉克斯」——拉紧的绳子一「拉」就「克」不住，慢慢变松；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 laxus（松的、松弛的）+ laxare（放松、解开）→ 英语 lax；核心义「失去张力」，由物理上的松弛引申到规章、态度与结构上的不严。

sensesIntro.en: Lax starts as the physical slackness of a rope, then loosens rules and discipline, then attention, then structure, and finally serves as a technical term in medicine.
sensesIntro.cn: lax 先是绳子物理上的松弛，继而指规章与纪律的放松，再到注意力的马虎、结构的松散，最后是医学中的专业用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rubber band that has lost its tension and sags.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根失去张力、松垂下来的橡皮筋。

branches.en: Rules held loosely are rules not enforced.
branches.cn: 被松松握着的规则就是没被执行的规则。

branches.en: Loose attention lets mistakes through.
branches.cn: 注意力一松，错误就漏了进来。

branches.en: The physical sense is the root of all the others.
branches.cn: 物理义项是其他所有义项之根。

branches.en: Careless work and a loose argument both fail to hold their shape.
branches.cn: 马虎的工作与松散的论证都维持不住形状。

branches.en: Medicine keeps the oldest sense in muscle and bowel.
branches.cn: 医学在肌肉与肠道上保留了最古老的义项。

intro.en: Lax is a bare Latin adjective with little internal structure, though its family grew through Latin suffixes such as -itas and -ativus.
intro.cn: lax 是一个几乎没有构词层次的拉丁形容词，它的词族是通过 -itas、-ativus 等拉丁后缀生长起来的。

latinIntro.en: Latin laxus means loose, and laxare means to loosen, with laxitas and laxativus as derived nouns and adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laxus 意为松散，laxare 意为放松，并由此派生名词 laxitas 与形容词 laxativus。

items.example: Laxus is the direct source of lax.
items.exampleCN: laxus 是 lax 的直接来源。

items.example: Laxare adds the action of letting go of tension.
items.exampleCN: laxare 添上松开张力的动作。

items.example: Laxitas is behind the English word laxity.
items.exampleCN: 英语 laxity 源自 laxitas。

items.example: Laxativus grows into laxative.
items.exampleCN: laxativus 发展为 laxative。

items.example: Lax carries both the physical and the moral sense.
items.exampleCN: lax 兼具物理与道德两个层面的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms laxity.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成 laxity。

items.example: Laxity is the formal noun of lax.
items.exampleCN: laxity 是 lax 的正式名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质的抽象名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms laxness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 laxness。

items.example: Laxness is the plainer noun of the quality.
items.exampleCN: laxness 是表示这种性质的较朴素的名词。

items.meaning: a medicine that loosens the bowels
items.example: Laxative shows the same loosening stem.
items.exampleCN: laxative 展示了同一个「放松」词干。

definition_zh: 小传单；宣传册；小叶；叶状结构
definition_en: a small printed sheet of paper giving information, or a small leaf-like part of a plant
core_image: 像一片小叶子那样薄薄的纸页，折一折就能塞进手里
scene: 公园入口，志愿者把薄薄的宣传纸页递给每位游客。At the park gate, a volunteer handed a thin leaflet to every visitor.
sceneCN: 这里 leaflet 是「小传单」（第 1 个义项：零星宣传用的薄纸页）；句意：公园入口，志愿者把薄薄的宣传纸页递给每位游客。

pos.zh: 小传单；宣传册；(植物)小叶

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「叶子」；加指小后缀 -let 得到「小叶、薄纸页」
leaf 加形容词后缀 -y，义为「多叶的；枝叶茂盛的」
leaf 加集合后缀 -age，义为「叶子（总称）」

senses.title: A small printed sheet
senses.definition: a single sheet or small folded sheet of paper giving information and handed to people
senses.definitionCN: 一张或一小张折页的纸，印有信息，分发给路人
senses.example: Volunteers handed out leaflets about the new recycling rules.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者们散发关于新回收规定的传单。
senses.why: The suffix -let means small, so a leaflet is a little leaf, a thin page like a fallen leaf.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -let 表示「小」，所以 leaflet 就是「小叶」，即像落叶一样薄薄的一页纸。

senses.title: A small leaf blade
senses.definition: one of the small separate blades that make up a compound leaf
senses.definitionCN: 复叶上分开的各个小叶片之一
senses.example: Each leaflet of the clover has a pale mark in the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 三叶草的每个小叶中间都有一道浅色纹。
senses.why: This is the literal plant sense: a leaf that is only a part of a larger leaf.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的植物义项：只是一片大叶子的一部分，所以叫「小叶」。

senses.title: Information with a medicine
senses.definition: the printed sheet packed with a medicine or device, listing its use and warnings
senses.definitionCN: 随药品或器械附带的印刷说明，列出用途与警告
senses.example: Read the leaflet inside the box before taking the tablets.
senses.exampleCN: 服用药片前请阅读盒内的说明书。
senses.why: The medical leaflet keeps the paper sheet sense but adds the duty of clear warnings.
senses.whyCN: 药品说明书保留「纸页」的意象，但增加了必须写清警告的用途，因此在医疗语境中固定下来。

senses.title: To give out printed sheets
senses.definition: to give leaflets to people in a place, often as a form of advertising or protest
senses.definitionCN: 在某个地点向人们发传单，常为宣传或抗议
senses.example: The students leafleted the whole neighbourhood on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们周日把传单发遍了整个社区。
senses.why: The noun became a verb by naming the action of dealing out its core object.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作动词，表示「把核心物品一张张发出去」的动作，这就是名词动用。

senses.title: A leaf-like flat part
senses.definition: a small flat part shaped like a leaf, as on some sea animals or a fold of metal
senses.definitionCN: 形状像叶子的小而扁的部分，如某些海洋动物身上的或金属折叠片
senses.example: The sea lily grips the mud with tiny leaflets along its stem.
senses.exampleCN: 海百合用茎上的小叶片状结构抓住泥沙。
senses.why: The shape sense extends the idea of a small leaf to any flat, leaf-shaped feature.
senses.whyCN: 形状义把「小叶」的形态推广到任何扁平、像叶子的小部件，因此出现在生物学和器械描述里。

senses.title: A thin layer in geology
senses.definition: a thin sheet-like layer in which some rocks or minerals split
senses.definitionCN: 某些岩石或矿物中可以劈开的薄片层
senses.example: Geologists mapped the dark leaflets of the slate.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家绘制了板岩中深色薄片层的分布。
senses.why: Geology reuses the thin page image for rock that comes apart in flat sheets.
senses.whyCN: 地质学借「薄纸页」的意象，形容岩石能劈成一片片薄层的样子。

intro.en: Leaflet is a native English compound: leaf plus the diminutive suffix -let, first recorded in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: leaflet 是英语本土构成的复合词：leaf（叶子）加指小后缀 -let，首见于十九世纪。

items.en: Leaf names the green blade of a plant.
items.cn: 古英语 leaf 指植物的绿色叶片。

items.en: The diminutive suffix -let enters English from French forms such as -et.
items.cn: 指小后缀 -let 经由法语形式（如 -et）进入英语，表示「小」。

items.en: Botanists use leaflet for a small blade of a compound leaf.
items.cn: 植物学家用 leaflet 指复叶上的小叶片。

items.en: A printed sheet comes to be called a leaflet, linking paper to fallen leaves.
items.cn: 印刷页开始被称为 leaflet，把纸张与落叶联系起来。

items.en: Leaflet also works as a verb for handing out such sheets.
items.cn: 现代英语里 leaflet 又用作动词，表示散发这种纸页。

note.en: Leaflet is a small leaf of paper or plant; its family is leaf and leafy, its neighbours are other kinds of printed pages.
note.cn: leaflet 是一片「小叶」，既可以是叶子也可以是纸页；同族有 leaf 与 leafy，近邻是各种印刷纸页。

entries.definition: a flat green part of a plant

entries.definition: having many leaves

entries.definition: leaves taken together as a mass

entries.definitionCN: 同用 -let 指小后缀，指小册子

entries.definition: a small pill or slab
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自 Latin tabula

entries.definitionCN: 近义：几页装订简单的小册子

entries.definition: a small magazine with pictures about a place or service

entries.definition: a single printed sheet for advertising

normalIntro.en: Leaflet is leaf plus -let, so it is a little leaf, and a printed sheet is paper thin as a leaf.
normalIntro.cn: leaflet 就是 leaf 加 -let，意思是「小叶」；而印刷纸页薄得像叶子，所以也叫 leaflet。

normal.en: Hand out leaflets at the station means to give printed sheets to people.
normal.cn: hand out leaflets 就是在车站向路人发宣传纸页。

normal.en: A leaflet campaign spreads a message through paper rather than screens.
normal.cn: a leaflet campaign 是靠纸页而不是屏幕来传播信息。

normal.en: The diminutive -let also builds booklet and droplet.
normal.cn: 指小后缀 -let 还能构成 booklet、droplet，都是「小」。

normal.en: In botany, one leaflet is one blade of a compound leaf.
normal.cn: 在植物学里，一个 leaflet 就是复叶上的一枚小叶片。

normal.en: Compare flyer: a leaflet may be folded and longer, a flyer is usually one loose sheet.
normal.cn: 对比 flyer：leaflet 可折页、篇幅更长，flyer 通常只是一张散页。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf-shaped paper pressed into a passerby hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张叶子形状的纸被塞进路人手里。

abstract.en: Think of a clover, where each small blade is a leaflet.
abstract.cn: 想象一株三叶草，每一枚小叶片都是一个 leaflet。

abstract.en: See a medicine box with a folded sheet slid under the lid.
abstract.cn: 想象药盒盖下压着一张折好的说明纸。

examples.en: The museum gives visitors a free leaflet with a map.
examples.cn: 博物馆向游客免费提供带地图的传单。

examples.en: Climate activists leafleted the shopping centre on Saturday.
examples.cn: 环保人士周六在购物中心散发传单。

examples.en: Each leaflet of the fern is divided into fine lobes.
examples.cn: 蕨类植物的每片小叶都分成细小的裂片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「理弗来特」——把道理印在纸上，一张张递过去；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 leaf（叶子）+ 法语系指小后缀 -let（小的）→ leaflet，字面义「小叶」，再由薄如叶的纸页引申出「传单」义。

sensesIntro.en: Leaflet starts from a small leaf, becomes a leaf-thin printed sheet, and then spreads by shape and use into medicine sheets, flat parts, and rock sheets.
sensesIntro.cn: leaflet 从小叶出发，变成薄如叶的纸页，再按形状与用途扩散到说明书、叶状小片和岩薄层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny leaf, so thin it could be a page of paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚小小的叶子，薄得可以当作一页纸。

branches.en: The printed sheet is the everyday sense for most readers.
branches.cn: 印刷纸页是大多数读者最熟悉的日常义项。

branches.en: The plant blade keeps the most literal meaning.
branches.cn: 植物的小叶保留最字面的含义。

branches.en: Medicine inserts and leafleting both deal out thin pages.
branches.cn: 药品说明书与散发传单都是把薄纸页发出去或递给读者。

branches.en: Both a plant blade and a flat animal part share the leaf shape.
branches.cn: 植物小叶与动物身上的叶状小片共享「叶形」。

branches.en: A paper leaflet and a rock leaflet both split into flat thin layers.
branches.cn: 纸质传单与岩薄片都具有平、薄、成层的共同特征。

intro.en: Leaflet is a native compound built on leaf with the diminutive suffix -let.
intro.cn: leaflet 是以 leaf 为词根、加指小后缀 -let 构成的本土复合词。

latinIntro.en: Leaflet has no Latin ancestor, but its suffixes echo the Latin use of diminutives and the family of folium, leaf.
latinIntro.cn: leaflet 本身没有拉丁语祖先，但它的后缀呼应拉丁语爱用指小词的习惯，同义拉丁词根则是 folium（叶）。
