基础词，义为「茎；梗」；单独也可指叶柄
botanical term，用拉丁词根 petiolus 构成的「叶柄」正式学名
leaf 加 -y，义为「多叶的」；与叶相关的同族词

senses.title: The stalk of a leaf
senses.definition: the part of a plant that carries a leaf and joins its blade to the stem
senses.definitionCN: 植物上托着叶片、把叶片连到主茎上的部分
senses.example: The leaves hang from long leafstalks.
senses.exampleCN: 叶子从长长的叶柄上垂下。
senses.why: Leaf plus stalk names the exact plant part: the stalk that belongs to a leaf.
senses.whyCN: leaf 加 stalk 直接点出部位：属于叶子的那根梗，所以是「叶柄」。

senses.title: An edible leaf stem
senses.definition: the stalk of a vegetable leaf, often cooked and eaten separately from the blade
senses.definitionCN: 蔬菜叶子的梗，常与叶片分开烹饪食用
senses.example: Slice the leafstalks of the chard and fry them first.
senses.exampleCN: 把莙荙菜的叶梗切片，先下锅炒。
senses.why: In cooking the same part becomes food, so the word shifts from botany to the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 在厨房里这同一部位成了食材，词义因此从植物学转向烹饪。

senses.title: The handle of a leaf blade
senses.definition: a stem that lets a leaf turn toward the light and hold its weight
senses.definitionCN: 让叶片转向光线并承托其重量的梗
senses.example: A twisted leafstalk turns the blade away from the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 扭弯的叶柄让叶片转离墙面。
senses.why: This sense focuses on function: the stalk works like a handle for the leaf.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项强调功能：叶柄就像叶片的手柄，能转动角度、支撑重量。

senses.title: A slender support in general
senses.definition: any thin stem-like support that holds a flat part in place
senses.definitionCN: 任何一种托住扁平部分的细长支撑物
senses.example: The model lotus was fixed to a leafstalk of green wire.
senses.exampleCN: 模型莲花被固定在用绿色铁丝做的叶柄上。
senses.why: The picture of a thin stalk holding a blade extends to any thin support.
senses.whyCN: 「细梗托着叶片」的画面可以推广到任何细长的支撑结构。

senses.title: A point of breakage on a leaf
senses.definition: the joint where a leaf easily separates from the plant
senses.definitionCN: 叶片很容易从植株上脱落的那处接缝
senses.example: A yellow leafstalk marks where the diseased leaf will drop.
senses.exampleCN: 发黄的叶柄处标示出病叶将要掉落的位置。
senses.why: Because the stalk is the leaf joint, it also marks where a leaf lets go.
senses.whyCN: 因为叶柄就是叶片与植株的接缝，它自然也标示了叶子脱落的部位。

intro.en: Leafstalk is a transparent English compound of native leaf and stalk; both words are old, and the compound names the plant part directly.
intro.cn: leafstalk 是透明的英语复合词，由本土词 leaf 与 stalk 组合而成；两词都很古老，合成后直接命名植物部位。

items.en: Leaf means the blade of a plant.
items.cn: 古英语 leaf 指植物的叶片。

items.en: Stalca, the ancestor of stalk, means the stem or stalk of a plant.
items.cn: stalk 的前身 stalca 指植物的茎或梗。

items.en: Writers join leaf and stalk into leafstalk to name the petiole plainly.
items.cn: 近代英语把 leaf 与 stalk 连写，用大白话命名叶柄。

items.en: Botany keeps petiole as the learned term, leaving leafstalk to everyday description.
items.cn: 植物学沿用拉丁语来源的 petiole 作为正式术语，leafstalk 留给日常描述。

items.en: The spelling leaf stalk is also common, like leaf mould and leaf litter.
items.cn: 分写的 leaf stalk 也很常见，与 leaf mould、leaf litter 等写法一致。

note.en: Leafstalk joins the leaf family to the stalk family, while botany uses petiole and cooks speak of stems.
note.cn: leafstalk 把「叶」词族与「梗」词族连接起来；植物学另有 petiole，厨房里则常说 stem。

entries.definition: the flat green blade of a plant
a long thin stem of a plant
the main support of a plant
entries.definitionCN: 同族概念：植物的主茎，是叶柄的连接处

entries.definition: the stalk of a bean plant
entries.definitionCN: 同构词，豆类的茎，同用 -stalk 结构

entries.definition: a small leaf or a printed sheet
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近的叶类复合词，词源构成不同

entries.definition: the botanical name for a leaf stalk
entries.definitionCN: 近义：植物学正式术语「叶柄」

entries.definition: a thin stalk of a plant, often edible
entries.definitionCN: 近义：细梗；常指可食用的菜梗

entries.definition: the first new growth of a plant

normalIntro.en: Leafstalk reads like a label: the stalk that carries a leaf, so the whole word is its own definition.
normalIntro.cn: leafstalk 本身就是一张标签：托着叶子的梗，整个词就是它的定义。

normal.en: A leafstalk is the thin green stick under a leaf, like a personal handle.
normal.cn: leafstalk 就是叶子下面那根细绿梗，像叶片自带的把手。

normal.en: Botanists call the same part the petiole.
normal.cn: 植物学家把同一部位叫作 petiole。

normal.en: Stalk also survives in beanstalk and the story of the giant beanstalk.
normal.cn: stalk 还活在 beanstalk 里，也就是传说中的豆茎。

normal.en: Cutting the leafstalk of chard leaves the bright blade free.
normal.cn: 把莙荙菜的叶柄切下，鲜艳的叶片就剩下了。

normal.en: The base of the leafstalk is where a leaf finally breaks away.
normal.cn: 叶柄基部正是叶子最后脱落的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny green hand holding a leaf up to the sun.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小小的绿手把叶子举向太阳。

abstract.en: See two boats joined by a thin rope at the water.
abstract.cn: 想象两艘船被一根细绳系在水面上，中间那根绳就是叶柄。

abstract.en: Think of a pen whose thin neck means the blade turns easily.
abstract.cn: 想象一支细颈的笔，颈部一扭，笔尖便转向别处。

examples.en: Grasp the leafstalk gently so the blade does not tear.
examples.cn: 轻轻捏住叶柄，以免叶片被撕破。

examples.en: The rhubarb leafstalks turned red in the cold spring.
examples.cn: 寒冷的春天里，大黄的叶梗变成了红色。

examples.en: Bend the leafstalk to check how firmly the leaf is held.
examples.cn: 弯一弯叶柄，看看叶子能稳住多大的力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「里夫斯托克」——叶子（leaf）坐在一条细「斯托克」上，那条梗就是叶柄；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 leaf（叶子）+ 古英语 stalca（茎、梗，今作 stalk）→ leafstalk，合起来就是「托着叶子的梗」，即叶柄。

sensesIntro.en: Leafstalk always names the thin stem that holds a leaf: first the plant part, then its edible form, its handle role, its extended use, and its breaking point.
sensesIntro.cn: leafstalk 始终指托住叶子的细梗：先是植物部位，然后是可食用的菜梗、手柄作用、延伸用法与脱落处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin stalk holding up a leaf blade.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细梗撑起一枚叶片。

branches.en: The plant part is the literal botanical sense.
branches.cn: 植物部位是最字面的植物学义项。

branches.en: The edible stem sense moves from the garden to the kitchen.
branches.cn: 可食用菜梗义项把词从菜园带到厨房。

branches.en: Seeing the stalk as a handle explains why leaves can turn.
branches.cn: 把叶柄看作手柄，就能解释叶片为何能转动。

branches.en: Any thin support copies the shape of a plant leafstalk.
branches.cn: 任何细长支撑都在模仿植物叶柄的形状。

branches.en: As the leaf joint, the stalk is also the place of falling.
branches.cn: 叶柄既是连接点，也标记着叶片脱落的位置。

intro.en: Leafstalk is a two-part native English compound whose parts are both everyday words.
intro.cn: leafstalk 是由两个日常单词拼成的英语复合词，两部分都很直白。

latinIntro.en: Leafstalk has no Latin etymology of its own; the Latin-based learning word for the same plant part grew on folium and petiolus.
latinIntro.cn: leafstalk 本身没有拉丁词源；同一植物部位的拉丁系学名则长在 folium（叶）与 petiolus（梗）上。

items.meaning: the flat green blade of a plant
items.example: Leaf names the blade the stalk carries.
items.exampleCN: leaf 指叶柄所托起的叶片。

items.example: Stalk names the thin stem under a leaf.
items.exampleCN: stalk 指叶子下面的细梗。

items.example: Leafstalk is both parts joined.
items.exampleCN: leafstalk 就是两部分连写。

items.example: Leafstalks are visible along the stem.
items.exampleCN: 叶柄沿着茎一条条可见。

items.example: Petiole is the learned word for leafstalk.
items.exampleCN: petiole 是 leafstalk 的学名。

items.meaning: the main support of a plant
items.example: Stem is the thicker part a leafstalk joins.
items.exampleCN: stem 是叶柄所连接的较粗部分。

items.example: Beanstalk uses the same stalk pattern.
items.exampleCN: beanstalk 用的是同样的 stalk 结构。

items.example: Leafy plants need sturdy supports.
items.exampleCN: 多叶的植物需要结实的支撑。

items.example: Rhubarb is grown for its leafstalks.
items.exampleCN: 大黄正是为它的叶梗而种植。

latinEntries.exampleCN: folium 衍生出 folio 一词族。

latinEntries.meaning: a little stalk, a leaf stalk
latinEntries.example: Petiolus is the source of petiole.
latinEntries.exampleCN: petiolus 是 petiole 的来源。

definition_en: a long thin strap tied to an animal to keep it under control, or the power to control something
core_image: 一条细绳拴在狗颈圈上，绳的另一端握在人手里
scene: 清晨的河岸，主人攥紧绳子，让小狗靠近身旁。On the riverside at dawn, the owner pulled the leash tight to keep the puppy beside her.
sceneCN: 这里 leash 是「牵引绳」（第 1 个义项：拴住动物的皮带）；句意：清晨的河岸，主人攥紧绳子，让小狗靠近身旁。

collocations.phrase: keep a dog on a leash

derivatives.zh: leash 加 -ed，义为「拴着绳的；用皮带系住的」
un-（解除）加 leash，义为「解开皮带；释放」
unleash 加 -ed，义为「被释放的；不受约束的」

senses.title: A strap for an animal
senses.definition: a long thin strap attached to a collar that lets a person control an animal
senses.definitionCN: 系在颈圈上、让人能控制动物的细长皮带
senses.example: She clipped the leash to the dog collar.
senses.exampleCN: 她把牵引绳扣在狗颈圈上。
senses.why: The core image is a strap and a hand: one end tied, one end held.
senses.whyCN: 核心画面就是一条皮带和一只手：一头系住，一头握住。

senses.title: Control over someone
senses.definition: the power to limit or direct the actions of a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 限制或指挥某人、某群体行动的力量
senses.example: The board keeps a tight leash on spending.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会严密控制着开支。
senses.why: If a strap can keep an animal close, it can also stand for any limit on freedom.
senses.whyCN: 绳子能把动物拴近，就能比喻对自由的任何限制，于是引申为「约束」。

senses.title: To put a strap on
senses.definition: to fasten a leash to an animal or attach an animal with a leash
senses.definitionCN: 给动物系上牵引绳，或用绳把动物拴住
senses.example: He leashed the dog before opening the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他打开大门前先把狗拴上了绳。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb naming the act of adding the strap.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，表示「把牵引绳加上去」这一动作。

senses.title: A group of three
senses.definition: a set of three hounds or other animals tied or hunting together
senses.definitionCN: 猎场上拴在一起或一起狩猎的三只猎犬等动物
senses.example: The huntsman brought a leash of hounds to the field.
senses.exampleCN: 猎手带了一组三只猎犬来到场地。
senses.why: Old hunting counted working animals in threes, and the rope that tied them gave the group its name.
senses.whyCN: 古时狩猎按「三只」计算工作犬，拴住它们的绳索名字就转成了这组动物的量称。

senses.title: A cord in weaving
senses.definition: a cord or loop used in a loom to lift the threads
senses.definitionCN: 织机上用来提起经纱的绳或环
senses.example: One broken leash in the loom spoiled the pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 织机上一根综绳断了，花纹就乱了。
senses.why: The name for a controlling cord spread to the cords that control threads in a loom.
senses.whyCN: 「控制用的绳」这一叫法延伸到织机里控制纱线的综绳。

intro.en: Leash comes from Old French lesse, a thong or strap, itself from Latin laxare, to loosen.
intro.cn: leash 来自古法语 lesse（皮条、带子），源头是拉丁语 laxare（放松、松开）。

items.en: Laxare means to loosen or let go slack.
items.cn: laxare 意为放松、把绳子放长。

items.en: Lesse names a thong or long strap.
items.cn: lesse 指皮条或长带。

items.en: Lees becomes leash, a thong for leading a dog.
items.cn: 中古英语 lees 逐渐写成 leash，指牵狗的皮带。

items.en: Hunting gives leash the sense of a group of three hounds.
items.cn: 狩猎语境给 leash 添了「三只一组猎犬」的量称义。

items.en: Leash is used figuratively for control, and unleash grows from the image of releasing the strap.
items.cn: 现代英语中 leash 常用于比喻控制，而 unleash 正是从「解开皮带」的画面长出来的。

note.en: Leash is a strap from Latin laxare; its family includes unleashing, and its neighbours are leads, tethers, and the idea of restraint.
note.cn: leash 是源于拉丁语 laxare 的皮带；同族有 unleash，近邻是 lead、tether 以及「约束」这类概念。

entries.definition: to release from a leash or let loose
entries.definitionCN: un- 加 leash，义为「解开皮带；释放」

entries.definition: tied or kept with a leash
to beat or tie with a rope
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，义为抽打或捆扎，词源与 leash 不同

entries.definition: to let liquid escape
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，义为漏出，词源不同

entries.definition: a contract to rent property
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，义为租约，词源不同

entries.definition: a strap for leading a dog
entries.definitionCN: 近义：牵狗用的皮带（英式常用）

entries.definition: a rope tying an animal to a fixed point
entries.definitionCN: 近义：把动物拴在固定处的绳

entries.definition: straps fitted to an animal for control
entries.definitionCN: 近义：套在动物身上控制其行动的挽具

entries.definition: the act of holding something back

normalIntro.en: Leash keeps the image of a loose strap: hold it and the animal stays near, drop it and things run free.
normalIntro.cn: leash 保留「松开的皮条」这一画面：握住它，动物就近；放下它，一切就放开了。

normal.en: On a leash means the animal is tied and under control.
normal.cn: on a leash 表示动物被拴着、在控制之下。

normal.en: To slip the leash means to escape control.
normal.cn: slip the leash 就是挣脱控制、溜之大吉。

normal.en: Unleash adds un- to mean let go, so unleash power means release it.
normal.cn: unleash 加 un- 表示「解开」，所以 unleash power 就是释放力量。

normal.en: Keep someone on a short leash means to watch them closely.
normal.cn: 「keep someone on a short leash」就是严加看管某人。

normal.en: Leash shares its family with leash law, the rule that dogs must be tied in public.
normal.cn: leash 还有 leash law 这个同族说法，指公共场所遛狗必须牵引。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tightening a strap as a dog pulls forward.
abstract.cn: 想象狗往前冲时，一只手把皮带绷紧。

abstract.en: See a manager holding a thin line tied to a whole team.
abstract.cn: 想象一位管理者手里牵着一根细线，另一端系着整个团队。

abstract.en: Think of the moment the clip snaps shut, and the world is held.
abstract.cn: 想象扣环咔嗒一声合上，一切就被牵住了。

examples.en: Dogs must be kept on a leash in this park.
examples.cn: 在这个公园里，狗必须拴着牵引绳。

examples.en: The new rules leashed the banks more tightly than expected.
examples.cn: 新规对银行的约束比预期更严。

examples.en: He slipped the leash and joined his friends downtown.
examples.cn: 他偷偷溜了出去，和朋友们在市中心会合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离实」——绳子让对方离得实在、跑不远；再联想「拎着绳」，与 leash 押韵；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 laxare（放松、松开）→ 古法语 lesse（皮条）→ 中古英语 lees、leash，核心义「可松可紧的皮带」。

sensesIntro.en: Leash starts as a physical strap, grows into the idea of control, then acts as a verb, and finally names grouped hounds and loom cords.
sensesIntro.cn: leash 从一条实物皮带出发，长出「约束」的抽象义，再转作动词，最后派生出猎犬量称与织机综绳的用语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a strap tied to a collar, with a hand at the other end.
core.cn: 核心意象：系在颈圈上的皮带，另一端握在人手里。

branches.en: The strap itself is the concrete sense.
branches.cn: 皮带本身是最具体的实物义项。

branches.en: Control is the abstract meaning grown from holding the strap.
branches.cn: 「约束」是从握住皮带长出的抽象义。

branches.en: The strap and the act of tying share one image.
branches.cn: 皮带与拴绳的动作共享同一个画面。

branches.en: Old hunting used one strap to tie three hounds together.
branches.cn: 古时狩猎用一根绳把三只猎犬拴在一组。

branches.en: A loom cord is another controlling strap in miniature.
branches.cn: 织机综绳就是缩小版的控制绳。

intro.en: Leash is a simple root word; English builds unleashes and unleashed on it with the prefix un-.
intro.cn: leash 本身是词根词；英语用前缀 un- 在它上面构出 unleash、unleashed。

latinIntro.en: Latin laxare, to loosen, is the distant ancestor, and it also gives English relax and lax.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 laxare（放松）是它的远祖，同一个词根还带给英语 relax 与 lax。

items.meaning: a strap, or to tie with one
items.example: Leash is the base noun and verb.
items.exampleCN: leash 既是名词也是动词的基础形式。

items.example: The prefix un- opens leash into unleash.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 leash 变成 unleash。

items.example: Unleash means take the strap off.
items.exampleCN: unleash 意为把皮带解下。

items.meaningCN: 表示「具有某种状态」的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ed forms leashed.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 leashed。

items.example: Leashed dogs are welcome.
items.exampleCN: 拴好绳的狗可以带入。

items.example: Leashes hang by the door.
items.exampleCN: 牵引绳挂在门边。

items.example: Lax and leash share the Latin origin.
items.exampleCN: lax 与 leash 共享拉丁语源头。

items.example: Relax keeps the same loosening idea.
items.exampleCN: relax 保留了同样的「放松」概念。

items.meaning: a rope that ties an animal
items.example: Tether is a near neighbour of leash.
items.exampleCN: tether 是 lease 的近邻词。

latinEntries.example: Laxare is the root of relax.
latinEntries.exampleCN: laxare 是 relax 的词根。

latinEntries.example: Laxus gives the English word lax.
